title: Research availability
description: Explore Recoup research, choose the right identifiers, and handle incomplete data.
body:
Recoup Research lets you discover artists and tracks, read current metrics,
explore audience and playlist activity, and capture recording measurements.
Authenticate with your Recoup API key or supported bearer credential. Recoup
manages the data connections; you do not need a separate data-service key.

Coverage varies by artist, recording, platform and metric. An empty result means
no matching data was returned; it does not prove an artist has no activity or audience.

## Choose an identifier

Search by name, inspect the matches, and pass the selected result's `id` to the
detail endpoints. Treat research IDs as opaque strings: do not parse them or
substitute a Recoup account UUID. Artist-name shortcuts use the first match;
select an explicit ID when names are ambiguous.

For portable recording references, store the ISRC and available Spotify or
Apple Music identifiers. Additional response fields and provenance labels may
vary as Recoup's data connections change. Preserve returned provenance for
traceability without using it to choose a data vendor.

## Current track statistics

Supply exactly one of `isrc`, `spotify_track_id`, or `apple_music_track_id`, plus
the required `source` (the platform, such as `spotify`). Recoup uses stored
Spotify measurements when available for an ISRC, and otherwise requests current
research data. Preserve `data_source` and capture timestamps when returned;
missing provenance remains unknown. A displayed play count is not a verified
royalty-bearing stream count.

## Research endpoints

| Method | Path | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/research` | [Search](/api-reference/research/search) |
| GET | `/api/research/albums` | [Albums](/api-reference/research/albums) |
| GET | `/api/research/audience` | [Audience](/api-reference/research/audience) |
| GET | `/api/research/career` | [Career activities](/api-reference/research/career) |
| GET | `/api/research/insights` | [Insights activities](/api-reference/research/insights) |
| GET | `/api/research/lookup` | [Spotify artist lookup](/api-reference/research/lookup) |
| GET | `/api/research/metrics` | [Current artist metrics](/api-reference/research/metrics) |
| GET | `/api/research/milestones` | [Milestones](/api-reference/research/milestones) |
| GET | `/api/research/playlists` | [Artist playlists](/api-reference/research/playlists) |
| GET | `/api/research/profile` | [Artist profile](/api-reference/research/profile) |
| GET | `/api/research/similar` | [Related artists](/api-reference/research/similar) |
| GET | `/api/research/track` | [Track details](/api-reference/research/track) |
| GET | `/api/research/track/playlists` | [Track playlists](/api-reference/research/track-playlists) |
| GET | `/api/research/tracks` | [Artist tracks](/api-reference/research/tracks) |
| GET | `/api/research/urls` | [Platform URLs](/api-reference/research/urls) |

## Understand the results

- Artist metrics are current snapshots. Save dated results to compare them over time.
- Related artists are unweighted; the accepted similarity axes do not change the ranking.
- Artist playlist `status=past` uses all-time scope and can include current placements.
- Career, insights and milestones expose available activities. They do not calculate a career score, create an AI report or guarantee a complete timeline.
- Album results can include track-shaped catalog entries. Do not assume every entry is a distinct album.
- Pagination and track-playlist filter behavior depend on the available data connection. Check the returned entries before assuming a filter was applied.

## Historical measurement jobs

`POST /api/research/measurement-jobs` supports `source: "historical"`
for Spotify backfill. It requires a card on file and returns queue counts with
`id: null`; enqueueing does not confirm capture completion. Recordings with an
existing historical research measurement can be skipped even when their history
is partial. Inspect the available dates before claiming complete coverage.
Current capture jobs return a snapshot ID.

## Costs and unavailable data

Successful research calls cost $0.05 (50,000 micro-dollar credits). Track-name
resolution can add separately charged lookup calls; reuse a selected research
ID when available. Historical enqueue itself does not deduct research credits;
capture work has its own balance and budget checks.

For `402 insufficient_credits`, show the returned `billingUrl`. Surface `429`
and unavailable-data errors; use bounded retries for transient failures and stop
when the request cannot be served. Recoup does not promise a `Retry-After` header
on these routes. Never fill a missing metric with an invented number or zero.

title: Create a new artist
description: End-to-end workflow to create, research and enrich a new artist account in a single session.
body:
This is the canonical recipe used internally by Recoup's chat agent. Follow it step-by-step to bring a new artist account up to "researched + enriched" parity from a sandbox or any external agent.

The chain is 8 sequential steps. Long deterministic chains executed from prose memory tend to drop steps — the agent reads the doc once, runs a couple of calls, and forgets the rest. To prevent that from a sandbox, **drive the work from a checklist file**: scaffold the artist's `RECOUP.md` with one checkbox per step before any API call, then tick each box and persist captured values back to the frontmatter as you go. The file becomes the workflow state, and a fresh turn can resume by reading it.

## Prerequisites

- `$RECOUP_API_KEY` (`x-api-key`) or `$RECOUP_ACCESS_TOKEN` (Privy Bearer JWT) for `api.recoupable.dev`
- `$RECOUP_ORG_ID` — the org the artist should belong to (recommended in sandboxes)
- An artist name to create (e.g. `ARTIST_NAME="The Weeknd"`)

Select one credential obtained through the approved real-account REST setup:

```bash
if [ -n "$RECOUP_API_KEY" ]; then
  AUTH=(-H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY")
elif [ -n "$RECOUP_ACCESS_TOKEN" ]; then
  AUTH=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $RECOUP_ACCESS_TOKEN")
else
  echo "Authenticate REST through the approved real-account setup flow." >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

Use your real account and selected organization. Do not create a disposable
`agent+` identity or paste credentials into the workspace file.

The flow has three phases, run from a single checklist file:

1. **Create + identify** — `POST /api/artists`, then find the canonical Spotify match
2. **Enrich** — `PATCH` the artist with image/label/socials, then read available Recoup research and search the web for narrative context and additional socials
3. **Synthesize + persist** — generate a knowledge-base report, save it (RECOUP.md tree or hosted URL), then optionally `PATCH` the `knowledges` array

## Step 0: Scaffold the workspace BEFORE any API call

Pick a slug, make the directory, and write the initial `RECOUP.md` template — frontmatter holds the values the chain captures (filled as you go); body holds the unchecked steps:

```bash
ARTIST_SLUG=$(echo "$ARTIST_NAME" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed 's/[^a-z0-9]\+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//')
ARTIST_DIR="artists/$ARTIST_SLUG"
mkdir -p "$ARTIST_DIR"

cat > "$ARTIST_DIR/RECOUP.md" <<EOF
---
artistName: $ARTIST_NAME
artistSlug: $ARTIST_SLUG
artistId:
spotifyArtistId:
spotifyProfileUrl:
imageUrl:
researchArtistId:
---

# $ARTIST_NAME

## Setup checklist

- [ ] 1. Create the artist (\`POST /api/artists\`) — capture \`account_id\` → \`artistId\`
- [ ] 2. Find canonical Spotify match (\`GET /api/spotify/search\`) — capture \`id\`, \`external_urls.spotify\`, \`images[0].url\`
- [ ] 3. PATCH artist with image + Spotify profile URL
- [ ] 4. Recoup research — resolve \`researchArtistId\`, read available profile/activity/playlists, then \`POST /research/web\`. Save responses and coverage gaps under \`## Research\`.
- [ ] 5. Pull Spotify catalog → write \`releases/{album-slug}/RELEASE.md\` per album + \`releases/top-tracks.md\`
- [ ] 6. Web search for additional socials (instagram / tiktok / twitter / youtube)
- [ ] 7. PATCH artist with discovered socials
- [ ] 8. Synthesize knowledge base — append it as \`## Knowledge base\` in this file

## Notes
EOF
```

The sandbox is already scoped to a single Recoupable organization (its repo _is_ the org), so artists live at the top level — there is no `orgs/` directory. Don't proceed to step 1 until the file exists on disk.

**After every step that follows, do two writes back to `RECOUP.md`:** tick the checkbox for the step you just ran (`- [ ]` → `- [x]`) and persist any captured value into the frontmatter. Later steps read those values from the frontmatter — never re-derive what's already saved.

## Resuming a partial setup

If `$ARTIST_DIR/RECOUP.md` already exists, do not re-scaffold and do not re-run completed steps. Read the file, find the first unchecked item, and resume from there using the values already saved in the frontmatter:

```bash
# Show the next unchecked step
grep -n '^- \[ \]' "$ARTIST_DIR/RECOUP.md" | head -1
```

If every item is checked, the artist is fully set up — confirm with the user before doing anything else.

## Step 1: Create the artist

```bash
ARTIST_RESPONSE=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/artists" \
  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg name "$ARTIST_NAME" --arg org "$RECOUP_ORG_ID" \
        '{name: $name, organization_id: $org}')")

ARTIST_ID=$(echo "$ARTIST_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.artist.account_id')
```

Capture `account_id` as `$ARTIST_ID` — every subsequent step needs it. `organization_id` is optional but should be included when running inside a sandbox so the artist is scoped to the right org.

See [Create Artist](/api-reference/artists/create) for the full request/response schema.

**After this step:** write `artistId: $ARTIST_ID` into the frontmatter and tick `- [ ] 1.` → `- [x] 1.` in `RECOUP.md`.

## Step 2: Find the canonical Spotify match

```bash
SPOTIFY=$(curl -sS -G "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/spotify/search" \
  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  --data-urlencode "q=$ARTIST_NAME" \
  --data-urlencode "type=artist" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10")
```

Inspect the returned candidates' names, profile links, images and catalog.
Set `SELECTED_SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID` to the verified match; popularity alone does not
establish identity. If candidates remain ambiguous, resolve that before saving
the artist's profile.

```bash
printf '%s' "$SPOTIFY" | jq '.artists.items[]? | {id, name, external_urls, images}'
```

If the verified artist is absent from the first ten results, repeat the search
with a more specific name or known catalog context and inspect the new results.
Do not substitute another artist. After verifying the candidate, export its fields:

```bash
: "${SELECTED_SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID:?Set the verified Spotify artist ID first}"
MATCH=$(printf '%s' "$SPOTIFY" | jq --arg id "$SELECTED_SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID" \
  '.artists.items[]? | select(.id == $id)')

SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID=$(printf '%s' "$MATCH" | jq -r '.id // empty')
SPOTIFY_PROFILE_URL=$(printf '%s' "$MATCH" | jq -r '.external_urls.spotify // empty')
SPOTIFY_IMAGE_URL=$(printf '%s' "$MATCH" | jq -r '.images[0].url // empty')

[ -n "$SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID" ] || { echo "No verified Spotify match for $ARTIST_NAME"; exit 1; }
```

Also keep `genres`, `followers.total`, and `popularity` from `$MATCH` for the KB report later.

See [Spotify Search](/api-reference/spotify/search) for the full query parameters and response schema.

**After this step:** write `spotifyArtistId`, `spotifyProfileUrl`, and `imageUrl` into the frontmatter, save `genres` / `followers.total` / `popularity` to the `## Notes` section, and tick `- [ ] 2.` → `- [x] 2.`.

## Step 3: Set basic profile + Spotify URL

One `PATCH` covers the image and the Spotify social URL. Use **uppercase** platform keys in `profileUrls` (the API matches platforms case-sensitively — see the reference table below).

```bash
curl -sS -X PATCH "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/artists/$ARTIST_ID" \
  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg image "$SPOTIFY_IMAGE_URL" --arg url "$SPOTIFY_PROFILE_URL" \
        '{image: $image, profileUrls: {SPOTIFY: $url}}')"
```

This single endpoint replaces what the chat tool chain runs as four separate MCP calls (`update_account_info` ×2, `update_artist_socials` ×2). Add `label` to the body only after verifying it in the research (step 4). See [Update Artist](/api-reference/artists/update) for the full body schema.

**After this step:** tick `- [ ] 3.` → `- [x] 3.`.

## Step 4: Run Recoup research

Resolve the verified Spotify artist to an opaque Recoup research ID, then read
available profile fields, activity and playlist placements. Coverage varies by
artist and platform: an empty successful response is a data gap, not a request to
warm a cache. Use a web search for biography, press and collaborations.

The four structured reads below cost $0.05 each when successful, or $0.20 total
(200,000 micro-dollar credits). Web research is billed separately; check the
current credit reference before running it. Check HTTP status before extracting
IDs or making dependent calls. This helper
allows at most three attempts for network failures or `5xx`, each with a
90-second timeout. A `402` surfaces `billingUrl`; a `429` stops the step and prints
`Retry-After` for a later manual retry; it does not wait or retry automatically. Leave the step unchecked on errors.

```bash
BASE="https://api.recoupable.dev/api"
research_request() {
  local path=$1 response body status attempt headers retry_after
  shift
  headers=$(mktemp) || return 1
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if response=$(curl -sS --max-time 90 -D "$headers" -w $'\n%{http_code}' \
      "${AUTH[@]}" "$BASE/research/$path" "$@"); then
      status=${response##*$'\n'}
      body=${response%$'\n'*}
      case "$status" in
        200) rm -f "$headers"; printf '%s' "$body"; return 0 ;;
        402)
          rm -f "$headers"
          printf 'Research needs credits: %s\n' \
            "$(printf '%s' "$body" | jq -r '.billingUrl // .error // "Check billing"')" >&2
          return 1 ;;
        429)
          retry_after=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="retry-after:" {sub(/^[^:]*:[[:space:]]*/, ""); sub(/\r$/, ""); print}' "$headers")
          rm -f "$headers"
          printf 'Research step stopped. Retry-After: %s. Resume manually when allowed.\n' "${retry_after:-not provided}" >&2
          return 1 ;;
        5??) ;;
        *) rm -f "$headers"; printf 'Research HTTP %s; resolve before resuming.\n' "$status" >&2; return 1 ;;
      esac
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then sleep "$((attempt * 2))"; fi
  done
  rm -f "$headers"
  echo 'Research unavailable after three attempts.' >&2
  return 1
}
```

### 4a: Resolve the research artist ID

```bash
LOOKUP=$(research_request lookup --get \
  --data-urlencode "spotifyId=$SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID") || exit 1

RESEARCH_ARTIST_ID=$(printf '%s' "$LOOKUP" | jq -r \
  '[.id, .artist_info.id] | map(select(type == "string") | select(test("\\S"))) | first // empty')
```

Save this value as `researchArtistId`. It is separate from the Recoup artist
account UUID and Spotify ID. Do not coerce it to a number or copy an older
saved research ID into it; re-resolve and verify older workspaces. If a successful
lookup has no usable `id`, record that gap and skip 4b–4d, then run 4e.

See [Artist Lookup](/api-reference/research/lookup) for the response contract.

### 4b–4d: Read available structured signals

```bash
if [ -n "$RESEARCH_ARTIST_ID" ]; then
  PROFILE=$(research_request profile --get \
    --data-urlencode "id=$RESEARCH_ARTIST_ID") || exit 1
  CAREER=$(research_request career --get \
    --data-urlencode "id=$RESEARCH_ARTIST_ID") || exit 1
  PLAYLISTS=$(research_request playlists --get \
    --data-urlencode "id=$RESEARCH_ARTIST_ID") || exit 1
fi
```

Inspect the fields actually returned. Profile data may be partial; `career` is
an available activity feed, not a guaranteed complete career timeline.
`playlists` returns `placements`, which may be empty. Do not turn missing data
into zero or infer a label, achievement or placement that is absent.

See [Artist Profile](/api-reference/research/profile),
[Artist Activity](/api-reference/research/career) and
[Playlist Placements](/api-reference/research/playlists).

### 4e: Search for narrative, press and collaborations

```bash

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg name "$ARTIST_NAME" \
        '{query: ($name + " biography press recent collaborations")}')") || exit 1
```

payloads, source links and coverage gaps under `## Research` in `RECOUP.md`, with
one subsection per request. Tick step 4 only after the successful reads and any
intentional structured-data skip have been recorded.

## Step 5: Pull the Spotify catalog

```bash

  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  --data-urlencode "id=$SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID")

ALBUMS=$(curl -sS -G "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/spotify/artist/albums" \
  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  --data-urlencode "id=$SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID")

# For each notable album, drill in (ALBUM_ID from $ALBUMS):
ALBUM_DETAIL=$(curl -sS -G "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/spotify/album" \
  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  --data-urlencode "id=$ALBUM_ID")
```

`$SPOTIFY_ARTIST_ID` is the value you exported in step 2.

See [Spotify Top Tracks](/api-reference/spotify/artist-top-tracks), [Spotify Artist Albums](/api-reference/spotify/artist-albums), and [Spotify Album](/api-reference/spotify/album) for full schemas.

**After this step:** populate the artist's `releases/` folder — write one `releases/{release-slug}/RELEASE.md` per album (album slugs are bare, `-ep` / `-single` / `-compilation` suffixes for other types) using the per-album `GET /api/spotify/album?id=$ALBUM_ID` response, and write the top tracks snapshot to `releases/top-tracks.md`. `RELEASE.md` is the 18-section master release-management document (project snapshot, identifiers, narrative, audience, DSP strategy, marketing, social, PR, visuals, physical/merch/touring, team, budget, KPI tracking, links hub, plus Outstanding Deliverables and a Document History log) — Step 5 fills the Spotify-derivable fields and leaves the rest as `⚠️ TBD`. The full template + the field-by-field Spotify mapping live in the [`artist-workspace`](https://github.com/recoupable/recoup-platform-plugin/tree/main/skills/artist-workspace) skill at `references/release-template.md`. Tick `- [ ] 5.` → `- [x] 5.`.

## Step 6: Search the web for additional socials

```bash
SOCIALS_SEARCH=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/research/web" \
  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg name "$ARTIST_NAME" \
        '{query: ($name + " official instagram tiktok twitter youtube")}')")
```

Parse the results to extract any new social URLs whose host matches the platform reference table below.

See [Web Search](/api-reference/research/web) for the request/response schema.

**After this step:** save the discovered URLs (one per platform) into the `## Notes` section so step 7 can read them without re-querying. Tick `- [ ] 6.` → `- [x] 6.`.

## Step 7: PATCH the artist with the discovered socials

```bash
curl -sS -X PATCH "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/artists/$ARTIST_ID" \
  "${AUTH[@]}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "profileUrls": {
      "INSTAGRAM": "https://instagram.com/...",
      "TIKTOK": "https://tiktok.com/@...",
      "TWITTER": "https://x.com/...",
      "YOUTUBE": "https://youtube.com/@..."
    }
  }'
```

Only include keys for platforms you actually found URLs for. The PATCH preserves existing socials for keys you omit, so this is safe to run incrementally.

See [Update Artist](/api-reference/artists/update) for the full body schema.

**After this step:** tick `- [ ] 7.` → `- [x] 7.`.

## Step 8: Synthesize the knowledge base

Combine the available structured and web research (`## Research` section), the Spotify catalog (`releases/`), and the discovered socials into a comprehensive markdown report. Recommended sections:

- Artist biography and origin
- Discography highlights (top tracks + key albums)
- Spotify presence (genres, listener count, notable playlists)
- Social media footprint
- Recent activity / press
- Notable collaborations and achievements

Append the report to the same `RECOUP.md` you scaffolded in Step 0 — add it as a `## Knowledge base` section below the checklist. The path is:

```
artists/$ARTIST_SLUG/RECOUP.md
```

This dovetails with the [`artist-workspace`](https://github.com/recoupable/recoup-platform-plugin/tree/main/skills/artist-workspace) skill's filesystem conventions, so future sandbox sessions can read both the checklist and the KB without needing a hosted URL.

**After this step:** tick `- [ ] 8.` → `- [x] 8.`. With every box ticked, the artist is fully set up.

## Platform key reference

`profileUrls` keys are **uppercase** platform identifiers, inferred from the URL host. Recognized platforms:

| URL contains                 | `profileUrls` key |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `spotify.com`                | `SPOTIFY`         |
| `instagram.com`              | `INSTAGRAM`       |
| `tiktok.com`                 | `TIKTOK`          |
| `x.com`, `twitter.com`       | `TWITTER`         |
| `youtube.`                   | `YOUTUBE`         |
| `apple.com`                  | `APPLE`           |
| `facebook.com`               | `FACEBOOK`        |
| `threads.net`, `threads.com` | `THREADS`         |

URLs that don't match any of these are silently skipped — they won't be saved.

## What this workflow doesn't enforce

There's no server-side orchestrator forcing each step to run in order — the chain is honor-system. The `RECOUP.md` checklist is what gives you determinism in practice: as long as you tick boxes and persist values after each step, a fresh turn (or a different agent) can pick up exactly where the last one stopped. If you skip a checkbox or skip the persist, the next turn won't know that step ran and may either redo it or, worse, treat downstream calls as ready when they aren't.

A few constraints to honor:

- **Run steps in order.** The frontmatter values written at one step are the inputs for later steps.
- **Don't continue past a 4xx/5xx without recovery.** Leave the box unchecked, write the error to `## Notes`, and resolve before resuming.
- **Treat the file as the source of truth.** If something isn't on disk, don't assume it ran.

Every Instagram scrape is followed by one batched profile run over the new commenters, which fills `avatar`, `bio`, `follower_count` and `following_count` on each fan; `region` is null unless the platform reports one. Supports pagination for large fan lists.

`last_comment_at` is the timestamp of the latest stored comment linked to that fan relationship, when the comment's author matches the returned fan. Missing or mismatched comment evidence returns `null`; it does not mean the fan has never commented. Profile refresh time and other engagement timestamps are not substituted. This is stored evidence, not a live scrape or exhaustive interaction history, and older relationship links are not guaranteed backfilled. Existing ordering, pagination and duplicate fan rows across relationships are unchanged.

The caller must be authenticated and have access to the artist. This field supports a report's Last heard column; it does not itself return comment bodies. title: Stream chat
description: Streams an agent loop running as a durable Vercel Workflow against the session's sandbox.
searchText:
Stream chat  Streams an agent loop running as a durable Vercel Workflow against the session's sandbox. Stream sandbox-driven chat (Vercel Workflow) Streams an agent loop running as a durable [Vercel Workflow](https://vercel.com/docs/workflow) against the session's sandbox. The agent uses sandbox-only tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `grep`, `glob`, `todo`, `task`, `ask_user_question`, `skill`, `fetch`) — no MCP or Composio. Requires a sandbox provisioned via [`POST /api/sandbox`](/api-reference/sandbox/create).

**Related endpoints**
- [`POST /api/chat/runs`](/api-reference/chat/runs) — the **headless** counterpart: it provisions its own session + sandbox and runs without a streaming client. Use that for tasks/cron/programmatic runs; use this for **interactive, streaming** turns on an existing chat.
- [`GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream`](/api-reference/chat/workflow-stream) — reconnect to an in-progress response.
- [`GET /api/chat/runs/{runId}`](/api-reference/chat/runs-status) — check **whether** a headless run finished (status, not content).

A new turn is separate from reconnecting. If the early active-run check finds an existing run whose status is running or pending, POST returns `409` before saving the new message or starting a new workflow. Keep the rejected text and attachments locally, reconnect with GET, and let the caller decide when to submit them again. Do not queue or automatically resend them, or delete persisted chat history to recover an unaccepted submission. Later start conflicts can also return `409` after work has started; inspect chat state before retrying. An unresolved startup reservation, unknown run status, failed status lookup or failed stale-slot clear returns retryable `503` before saving the submitted turn or starting a new workflow. Preserve the text and attachments for a later manual retry.

To make a reader disconnect leave the workflow running, send `?streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1` on this POST and every reconnect GET. Use `POST /api/chat/{chatId}/stop` for explicit cancellation; aborting the local reader is not confirmation that server work stopped. Only exactly one streamLifecycle query parameter with that exact value opts in. Omitted, empty, unknown or repeated parameters retain legacy disconnect cancellation. Chats Streaming POST /api/chat

title: Resume chat stream
description: Reconnects to an in-progress chat response without submitting another message. POST /api/chat starts a new turn: an existing live run returns 409, while…
searchText:
Resume chat stream  Reconnects to an in-progress chat response without submitting another message. POST /api/chat starts a new turn: an existing live run returns 409, while… Resume a chat response stream Reconnects to an in-progress chat response without submitting another message. POST /api/chat starts a new turn: an existing live run returns 409, while uncertain state or a startup reservation returns retryable 503. Returns a live Server-Sent Events stream while a response is being generated, or a `200` finish-only SSE stream when no active response exists or the run is terminal. The chat must belong to the authenticated account.

Send `?streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1` on both the initial POST and this reconnect GET to keep server work running when a reader disconnects. Use the authenticated Stop endpoint for cancellation; closing or aborting this reader alone does not confirm that the workflow stopped. Only exactly one streamLifecycle parameter with the exact value opts in; omitted, empty, unknown or repeated parameters retain legacy disconnect cancellation. Keep the existing `startIndex` cursor when reconnecting an already-read response.

**Related endpoints**
- [`POST /api/chat`](/api-reference/chat/workflow) — the interactive turn whose stream this resumes.

- [`GET /api/chat/runs/{runId}`](/api-reference/chat/runs-status) — check **whether** that run finished (status, not content). Chats Streaming GET /api/chat/{chatId}/stream

Stop the response currently being generated for a chat, freeing it to accept a new message. Idempotent — returns `stopped: false` when nothing is in progress. The chat must belong to the authenticated account.

The active slot is released only after cancellation is confirmed. Cancellation failure (502) or termination timeout (504) keeps it occupied; a later stop can retry. A successful no-active stop returns stopped: false.

When a workflow is still starting and has no cancellable run ID, Stop returns retryable `503` and retains the active reservation. It does not report `stopped: true`; retry Stop shortly. A local reader abort is not confirmation that server work stopped.

For readers using `streamLifecycle=explicit-stop-v1`, this authenticated endpoint remains the explicit cancellation path. Chats Streaming POST /api/chat/{chatId}/stop

## Date range and coverage

Set `days` to an integer from 1 to 366 days. For example, use `days=90` for a 90-day comparison period. `since` is the inclusive start of the current period; the previous period has the same length and immediately precedes it. End dates are exclusive.

A supported date range does not prove complete measurements or historical backfill. Inspect each recording's coverage and missing dates before using growth comparisons, and continue through pages while `pagination.has_more` is true. Missing measurements suppress growth; they do not establish zero streams.

The catalog playcount-history operation has a separate 31-day maximum. It reports saved Spotify playcount observations; this endpoint reports saved worldwide aggregate daily streams across reporting services. Neither is a royalty statement. These reads do not start provider collection.

title: Context Engine
description: Save and reuse evidence in an authorized Recoup workspace. Preview: this reference is verified against API source, not a completed hosted acceptance test.
searchText:
Context Engine  Save and reuse evidence in an authorized Recoup workspace. Preview: this reference is verified against API source, not a completed hosted acceptance test. Ingest, read, or compile context briefs Save and reuse evidence in an authorized Recoup workspace. **Preview: this reference is verified against API source, not a completed hosted acceptance test.** Actions require the corresponding database and workflow release; verification actions also require their feature to be enabled. Do not infer provider readiness, complete coverage, or a successful workflow from an accepted request schema.

### Create context

`ingest` creates or reuses a Spotify-track request and dispatches its durable workflow (202). The parser recognizes YouTube URLs, but ingestion still rejects them in this pilot. `ingest_release` stores a Spotify album locator; it does not automatically verify the release. `ingest_catalog` and `ingest_artist` refer to accessible Recoup records. `ingest_songwriter_name`, `ingest_company_name`, `ingest_campaign_brief`, and `ingest_supporting_text` store submitted context (200). Names and customer text are not verified identities or facts. Reuse an idempotency key only for the same intended input.

### Read, plan and inspect

`read` reads one request. For saved supporting text, HTTP and standard MCP also return a metadata-only `material_evidence` receipt identifying the current document, result and exact retained source version. It returns no submitted text, source location or signed access. `draft_origin` remains `not_recorded`: a retained customer assertion is not proof of its file origin or reviewed business facts. Unavailable material withholds those references. Delegated OAuth keeps its request-only response. `plan` plans modules from stored context; a plan is not authorization to collect data. `list_executions` and `read_execution` expose execution records. `list_catalog_members` pages saved members; `expand_catalog_members` materializes a bounded member page. These operations return 200. Request IDs, subject IDs and execution IDs refer to different records; use the IDs returned by the corresponding read rather than substituting an account ID. Catalog membership does not establish rights ownership. Use `plan_catalog_members` to plan a lookup for a page of current expanded catalog recordings, as described below.

### Plan a catalog lookup

A catalog manager can inspect which lookup would be proposed for recordings already expanded from an accessible catalog. This action reads the saved targets and returns a plan; it does not fetch recording matches, linked works or platform information.

Supply the existing catalog Context `request_id` and its catalog `subject_id`, one `module`, and optionally `organization_id`, `after_isrc` and `limit` (1–100, default 100). These IDs refer to different records: do not substitute the catalog ID, account ID or a member recording subject for the catalog Context subject.

| Preferred input | Lookup being planned | Legacy accepted input and returned module |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recording_candidates` | Unconfirmed recording candidates from an ISRC; a candidate is not an approved recording identity | `musicbrainz` |
| `recording_work_candidates` | Candidate works linked to a recording; no ownership or royalty-share verification | `mlc_recording` |
| `platform_metadata` | Available platform track information; no growth-metric or complete-coverage promise | `songstats` |

All six input values remain accepted. The three values in the last column are compatibility identifiers, not a promise that data sources are interchangeable. Each preferred/legacy pair returns the same page, raw module, executor, node key, state and reasons. Source and saved-plan provenance remain unchanged.

The 200 result is `ContextCatalogPlanningResponse`: `page`, `plan` and `collectionPermitted: false`. `page` includes `catalogId`, `catalogSubjectId`, `members`, `nextCursor` and `hasMore`. Each member retains `subjectId`, `kind`, `identityConfirmed`, `availableFields`, `reusableModules` and `isrc`. The saved ISRC-backed target flag does not verify an external recording match, rights or ownership. Only expanded recordings still present in the selected workspace's accessible catalog are returned; removed and not-yet-expanded members are excluded. Pass `page.nextCursor` as `after_isrc` when `page.hasMore` is true.

`plan` has one node per returned member, including `key`, `entry`, `subjectId`, `targetKind`, `module`, `executor`, `state`, `reasons`, `dependsOn`, `scope` and `executionStarted`. Node keys retain `{subjectId}:{legacy_module}`. This action supplies no permitted modules and does not reuse collection permission: every returned node is `blocked`, has `executionStarted: false`, an empty `dependsOn` and the reason `Server collection policy has not permitted this module`. An empty member page returns `plan: []` and still has `collectionPermitted: false`.

An executor name describes a planned implementation; it does not make that collector runnable. In particular, the platform-metadata collector is not connected to the trusted planned dispatcher. No provider/model call, execution claim, credit charge, new access grant or automatic catalog expansion is triggered. An accepted request or local fixture is not hosted customer-workflow acceptance.

### Release verification and review

`verify_release` and `verify_release_tracks` enqueue enabled verification workflows (202); disabled features or unmet readiness conditions return 409. `list_release_tracks`, `read_release_track_observations`, and `review_release_track_identities` inspect saved slots and identity evidence (200). Inspect the returned readiness, coverage and unresolved identity state before using a recording match. `list_release_cases`, `read_release_case`, `read_release_case_review`, and `review_release_case` read or record release-case review. A review requires the current fingerprint, a decision, and an idempotency key; it does not silently rewrite source evidence.

### Compile and save briefs

`brief` compiles evidence from up to ten completed or partial requests in one workspace without provider or model calls. Purposes are `creative_direction`, `playlist_pitch`, and `company_onboarding`. Creative direction prioritizes lyrics and artwork; playlist pitching prioritizes catalog/audio metadata. Inspect readiness, request_coverage, selected input versions and gaps. Briefs are evidence packets, not finished creative concepts or outreach. Compiled documents have accepted status and full or partial coverage; creative proposals and other document states are excluded by the current selector. Accepted is a saved-evidence status, not verification of identity or rights. `save_brief` freezes the server-compiled output, and `read_brief` retrieves that snapshot without recompilation. Newer evidence can supersede a snapshot without rewriting it; withdrawn evidence or removed scope can withhold its payload. All three actions return 200.

### Link retained evidence

`attach_evidence` links one exact retained `source_version_id` to 1–100 distinct existing targets: an artist, a professional, or a Context request/subject pair. Supply a stable `idempotency_key`; retry only the same version and targets with that key. Authentication supplies the actor. The receipt records relevance only; it does not confirm identity, rights or a business mandate. It creates no roster entry and makes no provider/model call or charge.

`read_evidence_attachment` reads one receipt by `attachment_id`. `list_evidence_attachments` reads a page for an exact source version. Pass `next_id` as `after_id` while `has_more` is true, including an empty page where protected receipts were withheld. Reads check current workspace access, source retention and independent target access. Evidence responses and domain errors are private and must not be cached. A later source version needs a separate association; these actions do not rewrite historical receipts. They require the matching evidence-association database and API release; accepted request syntax is not hosted availability.

### Scope and failures

Authentication determines the account. Optional organization_id selects an authorized organization workspace; request and subject ownership are checked again by the operation. Invalid request syntax returns 400, missing authentication 401, rejected organization access 403, and operation conflicts, unavailable evidence or disabled verification 409. No action accepts a caller-supplied account identity. Local schema tests do not establish hosted availability.

### MCP mapping

Standard MCP uses the `context` tool with the same action and fields as this REST request. The three evidence actions also have individually discoverable object-schema tools listed separately below; they are excluded from delegated OAuth connections. Delegated OAuth exposes the named tools below and supplies the action server-side; omit action from the named tool input. These registrations require the full `mcp:tools` grant, current ownership and fresh credential verification. Read-only is a tool annotation, not a guarantee of hosted readiness. Discover the actual tools in the connected client before use; this is a static source mapping, not a verified client catalog.

| REST action | Delegated OAuth tool | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_release_cases` | `list_music_release_cases` | Read-only hint |
| `read_release_case` | `read_music_release_case` | Read-only hint |
| `read_release_case_review` | `read_music_release_case_review` | Read-only hint |
| `review_release_case` | `record_music_release_case_review` | Writes or dispatches |

### Catalog case continuation

`save_catalog_case`, `read_catalog_case` and `list_catalog_cases` persist bounded catalog workflow artifacts as `customer_assertion` evidence. They are source contracts requiring the corresponding catalog-case database/API release; source tests and this reference do not prove deployment. No artist, ISRC, bank connection or ingestion request is required. Existing Context workspace authorization applies. These operations cannot register music, resolve a provider dispute, send correspondence or establish payment; `external_actions` is always `unsupported`.

Save uses a UUID `case_id`, `expected_revision` (0 for a new case), `idempotency_key`, and a portable version-1 snapshot. Its workspace must be the authenticated owner, its case ID must match, and its revision must equal the expected revision. A saved receipt advances the revision. Snapshots contain scope and dictionaries of sources, assessments, findings, actions, attempts and outcomes; IDs must be unique, source references versioned, dependencies retained and acyclic. Each collection is limited to 1,000 records; the artifact is limited to 1 MiB. Arbitrary JSON extensions accept finite JSON with at most 100 nested levels. Unknown fields and local `history` are rejected, not dropped. Use record `data` for typed workpapers. Action payloads require nonempty provider/operation/account/party strings, nonempty subject identifiers, a nonempty scope object and explicit disclosure/cost arrays. Expired historical authorization assertions remain readable; caller-recorded authorization never grants provider authority.

Replay an uncertain save with the same idempotency key, expected revision and unchanged snapshot. Re-read before editing a conflicting revision. Read supports an optional historical revision, and rechecks current access and retained Context source versions. Linked withdrawn sources and dependent records are withheld even in historical reads. A `partial` snapshot with `snapshot_usable_for_save: false` must be explicitly reassembled from permitted evidence before another save. A stale reference to an older source version requires a retained binding from this same case's earlier saved history; an imported stale record without that binding cannot be saved as though its provenance were known.

List defaults to 50 cases and accepts a 1–100 limit. Pass `next_id` as `after_id` while `has_more` is true. Storage orders by creation time and ID descending; the UUID cursor is an opaque case reference, not a sortable boundary by itself. Responses use private/no-store caching. All three operations are standard MCP only and excluded from delegated OAuth. Prepared, submitted, provider-accepted, observed-correct and bank-received remain separate assertions that need their own actual evidence; artifact storage certifies none of them. title: Generate a music video
description: End-to-end workflow to produce a vertical, social-ready music video — image, motion, caption — from an artist and a song.
body:
This is the canonical recipe used internally by Recoup's `create-content` background task. Two paths are documented below: the **async pipeline** that an LLM agent should use, and the **manual recipe** for humans (or for cases where you want to swap a single step).

## Hand it to your LLM

The fastest way to use this guide is to point an LLM at it directly — every page on this site is also served as raw markdown at the same path with a `.md` suffix, so models can fetch and follow it without parsing HTML:

```
Generate a music video for The Weeknd – "Blinding Lights" using
https://docs.recoupable.dev/workflows/generate-music-video.md
```

Swap in your own artist and song. The LLM will resolve the artist, kick off the async pipeline, poll until done, and pull back the final video URL.

## Running as an agent? Use the async pipeline

`POST /api/content/video` is synchronous and routinely takes 60–180s. Most agent shells (Claude Cowork, OpenAI tool calls, etc.) cap a single command at 30–60s and kill background processes when the shell exits — the manual recipe below is effectively un-runnable from those environments.

Use the async path instead — same five steps, run server-side:

```bash
# Trigger
RUN_IDS=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content/create" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg artist "$ARTIST_ACCOUNT_ID" --arg template "$TEMPLATE" \
        '{artist_account_id: $artist, template: $template}')" \
  | jq -r '.runIds[]')

# Poll (every ~10s) until COMPLETED / FAILED / CANCELED / CRASHED
RUN_ID=$(echo "$RUN_IDS" | head -1)
until STATUS=$(curl -sS "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/tasks/runs?runId=$RUN_ID" \
                 -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" \
               | jq -r '.runs[0].status') && \
      [[ "$STATUS" =~ ^(COMPLETED|FAILED|CANCELED|CRASHED)$ ]]; do
  sleep 10
done

# Read the output
curl -sS "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/tasks/runs?runId=$RUN_ID" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" \
  | jq '.runs[0].output'
# -> { videoSourceUrl, imageUrl, captionText, template, lipsync, audio: {...} }
```

Polling fits inside short shell timeouts and survives session restarts. See [Tasks Runs](/api-reference/tasks/runs) for the full status enum (`QUEUED`, `EXECUTING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, `CRASHED`, etc.) and the `CreateContentRunOutput` schema.

### Resolving `$ARTIST_ACCOUNT_ID`

`POST /api/content/create` needs the artist's `account_id`. Three calls:

```bash
ORG_ID=$(curl -sS "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/organizations" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" | jq -r '.organizations[0].id')

ARTIST_ACCOUNT_ID=$(curl -sS "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/artists?org_id=$ORG_ID" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r --arg name "$ARTIST_NAME" '.artists[] | select(.name == $name) | .account_id')
```

The artist record exposes both `id` and `account_id` (both UUIDs). Use **`account_id`** — `id` is the artist row's primary key, `account_id` is the underlying account that owns it. The two are easy to swap; you'll get a 404 from `/api/content/create` if you pass the wrong one.

## Where the song lives

Step 5 (and the async pipeline's lipsync mode) need a `song.mp3`. **Don't assume one exists, and don't assume the user has one locally.** Walk the agent through this fallback chain:

1. **Check the artist's sandbox repo first.** Each Recoup account has a backing GitHub repo. If the user has imported songs through Recoup, they live at predictable paths:

   ```
   .openclaw/workspace/orgs/{org-slug}/artists/{artist-slug}/songs/{song-slug}/{song-slug}.mp3
                                                                               /lyrics.json
                                                                               /clips.json
   ```

   Discover the repo with [`GET /api/sandboxes`](/api-reference/sandboxes/list) (returns `github_repo` and a `filetree`); fetch a file with [`GET /api/sandboxes/file?path=…`](/api-reference/sandboxes/file). **Binary files (`.mp3`, `.png`, `.mp4`) come back base64-encoded in the `content` field — decode before writing to disk.**

2. **If no song is in the sandbox, ask the user how to proceed.** Two options to offer:
   - *"Want me to fetch the audio from YouTube?"* — agent downloads via `yt-dlp` (or equivalent), saves locally; user is responsible for any rights / DSP-licensing implications.
   - *"Want to supply the song yourself?"* — user uploads / drops a path; agent reads from there.

   Don't pick a path silently. The cost of fetching the wrong song from YouTube (or fetching one at all) is enough that the user should make the call.

3. **Don't fall back to "use a placeholder track."** A music video without the song is not a deliverable.

## Manual recipe (humans + targeted overrides)

The rest of this page walks the same steps you can run by hand or call individually if you want to swap a single stage (different prompt for image, different motion, different caption length).

### Prerequisites

- An auth credential for `api.recoupable.dev`. Two options — pick one and use it for every call below:
  - **API key** (`recoup_sk_…`, recommended for sandbox / agent use): pass as `-H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY"`.
    - One-shot agent: `POST /api/agents/signup` with an `agent+{unique}@recoupable.com` email returns the key immediately.
    - Real-email signup: same endpoint with a real email mails a 6-digit code; complete with `POST /api/agents/verify`. See [Agents](/agents).
  - **Privy access token** (for end-user flows in chat/UI): pass as `-H "Authorization: Bearer $RECOUP_ACCESS_TOKEN"`.
  - The examples below use `x-api-key`. Substitute `Authorization: Bearer …` if you're using a Privy token.
- `$ARTIST_NAME`, `$SONG_TITLE`, `$SONG_LYRICS_CLIP` (a 1–2 sentence mood snippet)
- `$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` *(optional)* — an artist photo or album cover to seed the image; if your template's purpose is "show this exact image" (e.g. `album-record-store`), set this and skip image generation in step 2
- A `song.mp3` for step 5. **Don't ask the user for a local file** — fetch from the artist's repo via `/api/sandboxes/file`.
- `ffmpeg` installed locally for step 5

### Step 0: Scaffold the workspace BEFORE any API call

The `VIDEO.md` checklist *is* the workflow state — tick boxes and persist values back to the frontmatter as you go. To resume later, find the first unchecked box.

```bash
VIDEO_SLUG=$(echo "$SONG_TITLE" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed -E 's/[^a-z0-9]+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//')
VIDEO_DIR="videos/$VIDEO_SLUG"
mkdir -p "$VIDEO_DIR"

cat > "$VIDEO_DIR/VIDEO.md" <<EOF
---
artistName: $ARTIST_NAME
songTitle: $SONG_TITLE
template:
imageUrl:
videoUrl:
captionText:
finalVideoPath:
---

# $SONG_TITLE — $ARTIST_NAME

## Pipeline checklist

- [ ] 1. Pick template (\`GET /api/content/templates\` + detail) — capture \`template\`
- [ ] 2. Generate the base image (\`POST /api/content/image\`) — capture \`imageUrl\`
  - [ ] 2a. (Optional) Upscale image (\`POST /api/content/upscale\` with \`type: "image"\`)
- [ ] 3. Generate the video (\`POST /api/content/video\`) — capture \`videoUrl\`
  - [ ] 3a. (Optional) Upscale video (\`POST /api/content/upscale\` with \`type: "video"\`)
- [ ] 4. Generate the caption (\`POST /api/content/caption\`) — capture \`captionText\`
- [ ] 5. Compose 9:16 final with audio + caption (local \`ffmpeg\`) — capture \`finalVideoPath\`

## Notes
EOF
```

### Step 1: Pick a template (required: list **and** detail)

Templates carry the prompt, reference images, and styling that drive the rest of the chain — you can't write a good Step 2 prompt without them. List, pick, then fetch detail:

```bash
curl -sS "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content/templates" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.templates[] | "\(.id) — \(.description)"'

TEMPLATE="album-record-store"   # or artist-caption-{bedroom,outside,stage}

TEMPLATE_DETAIL=$(curl -sS "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content/templates/$TEMPLATE" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY")
```

**Templates that list "Requires: face image"** (e.g. `artist-caption-bedroom`) will fall back to their bundled reference images and produce a generic-likeness subject if you don't supply one — they don't 400. Pass `$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` if you want the model to preserve a specific artist's likeness, or omit it for a stock-feeling result.

See [List Templates](/api-reference/content/templates) and [Template Detail](/api-reference/content/template-detail).

**After:** write `template` into frontmatter, tick the box.

### Step 2: Generate the base image

Use the template's own prompt and reference images — don't write your own from scratch. The template encodes the visual style; freeform prompts almost always drift off-brand.

```bash
PROMPT=$(echo "$TEMPLATE_DETAIL" | jq -r '.image.prompt')
REFS=$(echo "$TEMPLATE_DETAIL" | jq -c '[.image.reference_images[]?]')
# $REFS is 5–15 URLs depending on the template — pass all of them via images[]

IMAGE_URL=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content/image" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg prompt "$PROMPT" --argjson refs "$REFS" \
        --arg ref "$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL" \
        '{prompt: $prompt, images: $refs} + (if $ref == "" then {} else {reference_image_url: $ref} end)')" \
  | jq -r '.imageUrl')
```

**Shortcut:** if `$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` is the exact image you want (e.g. an album cover for `album-record-store`, or a final editorial photo), set `IMAGE_URL=$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` and skip this call entirely.

**Avoid:** prompts that aim for a real artist's likeness. Veo (used in step 3) rejects celebrity-likeness images with a 422. Use the template's prompt as-is and let the reference images carry the style.

See [Generate Image](/api-reference/content/generate-image).

**After:** write `imageUrl`, tick the box.

### Optional: Upscale (image or video)

Same endpoint for both, swap `type`. Skip if you don't need the resolution bump.

```bash
# Image (after step 2)
IMAGE_URL=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content/upscale" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg url "$IMAGE_URL" '{url: $url, type: "image"}')" \
  | jq -r '.url')

# Video (after step 3) — same call, type: "video", reassign $VIDEO_URL
```

See [Upscale](/api-reference/content/upscale).

### Step 3: Generate the video

Pass the image and a short motion prompt. For lipsync, also pass a presigned `audio_url` to a song clip — the model will animate the artist's mouth.

```bash
MOTION=$(echo "$TEMPLATE_DETAIL" | jq -r '.video.movements[0] // "Slow camera drift, subtle subject motion"')

VIDEO_URL=$(curl -sS --max-time 360 -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content/video" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg image "$IMAGE_URL" --arg prompt "$MOTION" \
        '{image_url: $image, prompt: $prompt, aspect_ratio: "9:16"}')" \
  | jq -r '.videoUrl')
```

This call routinely takes 60–180s. **From a short-shell agent, use the async pipeline at the top of this page instead.** From a long-lived shell, output is an 8s clip. Step 5 loops it to song length.

See [Generate Video](/api-reference/content/generate-video).

**After:** write `videoUrl`, tick the box.

### Step 4: Generate the caption

```bash
TOPIC="Song: \"$SONG_TITLE\". Lyrics: \"$SONG_LYRICS_CLIP\". Artist: $ARTIST_NAME."

CAPTION_RESPONSE=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content/caption" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg topic "$TOPIC" --arg template "$TEMPLATE" \
        '{topic: $topic, template: $template, length: "short"}')")

CAPTION_TEXT=$(echo "$CAPTION_RESPONSE"     | jq -r '.content')
CAPTION_FONT=$(echo "$CAPTION_RESPONSE"     | jq -r '.font          // "/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc"')
CAPTION_COLOR=$(echo "$CAPTION_RESPONSE"    | jq -r '.color         // "white"')
CAPTION_STROKE=$(echo "$CAPTION_RESPONSE"   | jq -r '.borderColor   // "black"')
CAPTION_FONT_SIZE=$(echo "$CAPTION_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.maxFontSize  // 48')
```

`length` accepts `"short"` (default), `"medium"`, `"long"`, or `"none"` to skip. The four styling fields (`font`, `color`, `borderColor`, `maxFontSize`) are template-driven hints — Step 5 wires them into ffmpeg's `drawtext` so the burned-in caption matches the template's brand.

See [Generate Caption](/api-reference/content/generate-caption).

**After:** write `captionText`, tick the box.

### Step 5: Compose the final 9:16 video (local)

The API returns a 16:9 motion clip. Compose locally: crop to 9:16, overlay the song audio for the full duration, and burn in the caption with the styling from step 4.

```bash
curl -sS -o "$VIDEO_DIR/clip.mp4" "$VIDEO_URL"
SONG_PATH="$VIDEO_DIR/song.mp3"           # see "Where the song lives" above
FINAL_PATH="$VIDEO_DIR/final.mp4"

# Write caption to a file — drawtext reads it via textfile=, sidesteps shell-escaping (apostrophes, etc.)
echo -n "$CAPTION_TEXT" > "$VIDEO_DIR/caption.txt"

# Single-line filter graph — newlines inside -filter_complex are literal characters and break the [v] label
ffmpeg -y \
  -stream_loop -1 -i "$VIDEO_DIR/clip.mp4" \
  -i "$SONG_PATH" \
  -filter_complex "[0:v]crop=ih*9/16:ih,scale=1080:1920,drawtext=fontfile=$CAPTION_FONT:textfile=$VIDEO_DIR/caption.txt:fontcolor=$CAPTION_COLOR:fontsize=$CAPTION_FONT_SIZE:x=(w-text_w)/2:y=h-text_h-120:box=1:boxcolor=$CAPTION_STROKE@0.5:boxborderw=20[v]" \
  -map "[v]" -map "1:a" \
  -shortest -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  "$FINAL_PATH"
```

**After:** write `finalVideoPath`, tick the box. With every box ticked, the music video is complete.

## Step 6: Publish (optional)

Once the MP4 is rendered, push it to the artist's socials with the [Connectors API](/api-reference/connectors/list). One heads-up worth knowing:

- **TikTok URL ownership.** `TIKTOK_PUBLISH_VIDEO` (pull-from-URL mode) requires the source domain be verified in the TikTok dev portal. `fal.media` URLs will fail with `url_ownership_unverified` — use `TIKTOK_UPLOAD_VIDEO` instead, which accepts the same URL and uploads server-side.

---

The checklist is the source of truth — if a box isn't ticked, treat the step as not run.

Three calls: The artist record exposes both `id` and `account_id` (both UUIDs). Use **`account_id`** — `id` is the artist row's primary key, `account_id` is the underlying account that owns it. The two are easy to swap; you'll get a 404 from `/api/content/create` if you pass the wrong one. ## Where the song lives Step 5 (and the async pipeline's lipsync mode) need a `song.mp3`. **Don't assume one exists, and don't assume the user has one locally.** Walk the agent through this fallback chain: 1. **Check the artist's sandbox repo first.** Each Recoup account has a backing GitHub repo. If the user has imported songs through Recoup, they live at predictable paths: Discover the repo with [`GET /api/sandboxes`](/api-reference/sandboxes/list) (returns `github_repo` and a `filetree`); fetch a file with [`GET /api/sandboxes/file?path=…`](/api-reference/sandboxes/file). **Binary files (`.mp3`, `.png`, `.mp4`) come back base64-encoded in the `content` field — decode before writing to disk.** 2. **If no song is in the sandbox, ask the user how to proceed.** Two options to offer: - *"Want me to fetch the audio from YouTube?"* — agent downloads via `yt-dlp` (or equivalent), saves locally; user is responsible for any rights / DSP-licensing implications. - *"Want to supply the song yourself?"* — user uploads / drops a path; agent reads from there. Don't pick a path silently. The cost of fetching the wrong song from YouTube (or fetching one at all) is enough that the user should make the call. 3. **Don't fall back to "use a placeholder track."** A music video without the song is not a deliverable. ## Manual recipe (humans + targeted overrides) The rest of this page walks the same steps you can run by hand or call individually if you want to swap a single stage (different prompt for image, different motion, different caption length). ### Prerequisites - An auth credential for `api.recoupable.dev`. Two options — pick one and use it for every call below: - **API key** (`recoup_sk_…`, recommended for sandbox / agent use): pass as `-H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY"`. - One-shot agent: `POST /api/agents/signup` with an `agent+{unique}@recoupable.com` email returns the key immediately. - Real-email signup: same endpoint with a real email mails a 6-digit code; complete with `POST /api/agents/verify`. See [Agents](/agents). - **Privy access token** (for end-user flows in chat/UI): pass as `-H "Authorization: Bearer $RECOUP_ACCESS_TOKEN"`. - The examples below use `x-api-key`. Substitute `Authorization: Bearer …` if you're using a Privy token. - `$ARTIST_NAME`, `$SONG_TITLE`, `$SONG_LYRICS_CLIP` (a 1–2 sentence mood snippet) - `$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` *(optional)* — an artist photo or album cover to seed the image; if your template's purpose is "show this exact image" (e.g. `album-record-store`), set this and skip image generation in step 2 - A `song.mp3` for step 5. **Don't ask the user for a local file** — fetch from the artist's repo via `/api/sandboxes/file`. - `ffmpeg` installed locally for step 5 ### Step 0: Scaffold the workspace BEFORE any API call The `VIDEO.md` checklist *is* the workflow state — tick boxes and persist values back to the frontmatter as you go. To resume later, find the first unchecked box. ### Step 1: Pick a template (required: list **and** detail) Templates carry the prompt, reference images, and styling that drive the rest of the chain — you can't write a good Step 2 prompt without them. List, pick, then fetch detail: **Templates that list "Requires: face image"** (e.g. `artist-caption-bedroom`) will fall back to their bundled reference images and produce a generic-likeness subject if you don't supply one — they don't 400. Pass `$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` if you want the model to preserve a specific artist's likeness, or omit it for a stock-feeling result. See [List Templates](/api-reference/content/templates) and [Template Detail](/api-reference/content/template-detail). **After:** write `template` into frontmatter, tick the box. ### Step 2: Generate the base image Use the template's own prompt and reference images — don't write your own from scratch. The template encodes the visual style; freeform prompts almost always drift off-brand. **Shortcut:** if `$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` is the exact image you want (e.g. an album cover for `album-record-store`, or a final editorial photo), set `IMAGE_URL=$REFERENCE_IMAGE_URL` and skip this call entirely. **Avoid:** prompts that aim for a real artist's likeness. Veo (used in step 3) rejects celebrity-likeness images with a 422. Use the template's prompt as-is and let the reference images carry the style. See [Generate Image](/api-reference/content/generate-image). **After:** write `imageUrl`, tick the box. ### Optional: Upscale (image or video) Same endpoint for both, swap `type`. Skip if you don't need the resolution bump. See [Upscale](/api-reference/content/upscale). ### Step 3: Generate the video Pass the image and a short motion prompt. For lipsync, also pass a presigned `audio_url` to a song clip — the model will animate the artist's mouth. This call routinely takes 60–180s. **From a short-shell agent, use the async pipeline at the top of this page instead.** From a long-lived shell, output is an 8s clip. Step 5 loops it to song length. See [Generate Video](/api-reference/content/generate-video). **After:** write `videoUrl`, tick the box. ### Step 4: Generate the caption `length` accepts `"short"` (default), `"medium"`, `"long"`, or `"none"` to skip. The four styling fields (`font`, `color`, `borderColor`, `maxFontSize`) are template-driven hints — Step 5 wires them into ffmpeg's `drawtext` so the burned-in caption matches the template's brand. See [Generate Caption](/api-reference/content/generate-caption). **After:** write `captionText`, tick the box. ### Step 5: Compose the final 9:16 video (local) The API returns a 16:9 motion clip. Compose locally: crop to 9:16, overlay the song audio for the full duration, and burn in the caption with the styling from step 4. **After:** write `finalVideoPath`, tick the box. With every box ticked, the music video is complete. ## Step 6: Publish (optional) Once the MP4 is rendered, push it to the artist's socials with the [Connectors API](/api-reference/connectors/list). One heads-up worth knowing: - **TikTok URL ownership.** `TIKTOK_PUBLISH_VIDEO` (pull-from-URL mode) requires the source domain be verified in the TikTok dev portal. `fal.media` URLs will fail with `url_ownership_unverified` — use `TIKTOK_UPLOAD_VIDEO` instead, which accepts the same URL and uploads server-side. --- The checklist is the source of truth — if a box isn't ticked, treat the step as not run.

title: Upload a public file
description: Upload one supported file to public Supabase Storage under your authenticated account.
body:
Use this endpoint for files intended to be publicly accessible, including public
profile images and attachments that may be shared by URL. It accepts one file up
to **4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes)** and returns its name, MIME type, byte size and URL.

<Warning>
  The returned URL is public. Anyone with the URL can read the file without
  signing in. Authenticating the upload does not make the stored file private.
  Do not use this endpoint for confidential documents or private source audio.
</Warning>

## Send a file

Send exactly one credential: an API key or an existing Bearer token. The uploader
comes from the authenticated account; do not include `account_id`, `uploaded_by`
or another ownership override. This route requires an existing account.

```bash
curl --request POST 'https://api.recoupable.dev/api/upload' \
  --header "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" \
  --form 'file=@cover.png;type=image/png'
```

Let your HTTP client set `Content-Type` and its multipart boundary. Send exactly
one `file` part and no other form fields. The streamed request body is limited to
**4,259,840 bytes** (4 MiB plus 64 KiB of multipart overhead); the 4 MiB limit
applies to the file itself.

Supported types are JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, PDF, CSV, Markdown, plain text, JSON, MP3,
WAV, M4A and audio WebM. The OpenAPI reference lists the exact accepted MIME types.
HTML, SVG, executables and unspecified binary types are not supported. Server
signature, UTF-8 and JSON checks still apply even if a browser accepts the file
locally.

## Existing files and private media

New uploads use Supabase Storage, not Arweave. Previously issued Arweave links
remain readable; this endpoint does not migrate or delete existing objects.
Private Files in `user-files` and [release-pack source audio](/release-packs)
continue to use their separate private-storage workflows.

The public response includes `success`, `fileName`, `fileType`, `fileSize` and
`url`. A handled error includes `success: false` and `error`. A failed request
does not establish whether a previous upload succeeded; do not treat this as an
idempotent replacement API.

title: Music API migration
description: Use the current background music-generation API; distinguish unfinished specialized outcomes from retired REST paths.
body:
## Generate a song now

Use [`POST /api/music`](/api-reference/music/generate) with a prompt and lyrics.
It returns `202` with a generation record; poll
[`GET /api/music/{generationId}`](/api-reference/music/get) for completion and
the resulting audio URL. It does not return audio in the initial response.
See the current reference for accepted settings, account scope and credits.

## Former music routes

The six POST paths below are retired from the callable specification because
they have no implemented handlers in the current API. They are not aliases for
`POST /api/music`. Their specialized outcomes are not equivalent to ordinary
song generation and are not declared canceled by this correction.

| Former path | Current choice and remaining limit |
| --- | --- |
| `/api/music/compose` | Use the current generation API for a prompt-and-lyrics song. Composition-plan input and an immediate binary-audio response are not supported replacements. |
| `/api/music/compose/detailed` | Use generation status/result reads for the fields actually returned. Multipart audio and word-level timestamps are not established by that result. |
| `/api/music/plan` | No hosted structured-composition-plan replacement is established. A locally prepared plan is not a supported request field, and the old free-operation claim is withdrawn. |
| `/api/music/stream` | Poll for the completed audio URL. The current API does not establish playback of partial audio chunks while the song is generated. |
| `/api/music/video-to-music` | No hosted upload-video-to-soundtrack replacement is established. Do not send video files to the prompt-and-lyrics endpoint. |
| `/api/music/stem-separation` | No hosted stem-separation replacement is established. Generating a new song does not split an existing recording into stems. |

## What remains undecided

[Reconciliation #327](https://github.com/recoupable/mono/issues/327) retains the
specialized capability decisions. The current music-generation implementation
is tracked in [App #1992](https://github.com/recoupable/app/issues/1992) and
[API #848](https://github.com/recoupable/api/pull/848); it is not delivery of every
former capability. An agent or local skill may help prepare inputs, but that
does not establish a hosted route or compatibility with the former request.

This is a reference correction. No provider run or audio-quality check was
performed to make these availability statements.

title: Get comments
description: Read existing stored comments on posts linked to a creator the caller can access. Authenticate with exactly one x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer credential.
searchText:
Get comments  Read existing stored comments on posts linked to a creator the caller can access. Authenticate with exactly one x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer credential. Read saved comments on an authorized creator’s linked posts Read existing stored comments on posts linked to a creator the caller can access. Authenticate with exactly one x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer credential. Caller identity comes from authentication; artist_account_id is the required target creator UUID (the retained wire name), not a caller override. account_id and other unknown or repeated query parameters return 400.

Access uses direct roster, shared-organization and Recoup-administrator checks, plus endpoint-local self-creator and owning-organization-key reads. These read rules do not grant artist mutation permission. Missing and denied targets both return 403. Access is checked on each request; this is not an atomic guarantee against revocation during an executing request. Ownership follows the creator’s linked socials through the post, not the commenter’s social_id. Optional post_id is a stored posts.id UUID, never a URL, and only narrows the authorized linked-post set. An unrelated post or no linked socials returns an empty page; neither permits an unscoped read.

page defaults to 1 and limit to 10; omitted or empty values use these defaults. Both otherwise require positive integers. Larger positive limits are accepted and clamped to 100; pagination.limit reports the effective value. Requests must satisfy page × effective_limit <= 2147483647 or return 400. Comments are ordered by commented_at descending, then id descending. Counts use the same ownership/post filter. Offset pages are deterministic for a fixed dataset, not a frozen snapshot during concurrent changes. A page beyond the results can be empty while retaining a nonzero exact total; no results means total_pages=0. A missing exact count is a 500, not an invented zero.

Each result has only id, post_id, social_id, comment and commented_at. Saved nulls are preserved in the nullable fields; a missing comment author/text is not invented. The stored post join determines inclusion; nullable post_id describes the retained row projection, not permission to read unlinked rows. No joined profile, account or grant metadata is returned. GET success and errors use Cache-Control: private, no-store. Authentication failures are 401; lookup failures are a masked 500 with no unscoped/provider fallback.

This reads saved evidence and does not start scraping, enrichment, billing or comment-writing work. The existing link lookup reads at most 10,000 social links; stored reads do not establish complete ingestion/history, a live report, or the original customer weekly-report journey. The implementation is merged in API #1062; hosted/customer verification remains separate in Mono #327/app #2023. Content Posts & comments GET /api/comments

description: Trigger a scrape of one social profile. Use Get Artist Socials first to get the social id.
searchText:
Social scrape  Trigger a scrape of one social profile. Use Get Artist Socials first to get the social id.  Trigger a scrape of one social profile. Use [Get Artist Socials](/api-reference/artists/socials) first to get the social `id`. The response contains scraper run metadata; poll it with the [Scraper Results API](/api-reference/apify/scraper).

**Credits:** `50,000 + 10,000 × posts` micro-dollar credits per profile: $0.05 base + $0.01 per requested post. Omitting `posts` charges the 50,000 base, even when the selected platform fetches a default depth.

**What `posts` does per platform**

| Platform | `posts` | When `posts` is omitted |
|---|---|---|
| Instagram | ignored | the profile's latest posts (up to 12), always |
| TikTok | `resultsPerPage` | 1 video |
| YouTube | `maxResults`, `maxResultsShorts`, `maxResultStreams` (per content type) | 1 video, 0 Shorts, 0 streams |
| X / Twitter | timeline items; retweets and replies are fetched but not stored | 10 timeline items before filtering |
| LinkedIn | `maxPosts` on the posts actor (runs instead of the profile actor) | profile only, no posts |
| Threads | ignored | profile only |
| Facebook | ignored | profile only |

**What gets stored.** Webhook processing persists supported records from successful runs. Platform filtering, missing fields and budget-limited follow-ups can leave partial results:

- The profile: username, avatar, bio, follower and following counts, region. Served by [Get Artist Socials](/api-reference/artists/socials).
- One follower snapshot per social per day whenever the run reports a follower count (following and post counts too, where the platform reports them). Served by the `history` parameter of Get Artist Socials.
- Every returned post with its engagement (`views`, `likes`, `comments`, `reposts`, where the platform reports them). Served by [Get Artist Posts](/api-reference/posts/get).
- Instagram only: comments batches for already-known and newly discovered posts, then terminal profile batches for the returned commenters. Available profile fields are saved; completion and field coverage are not guaranteed. Served by [Get Artist Fans](/api-reference/fans/get).

**Fan discovery is one hop deep.** The commenter profile run is terminal: it never schedules comments or profile runs of its own. A normal single delivery can produce one profile run, two comments batches and two terminal commenter-profile batches. Five is a derived case, not a universal bound: retries, concurrent deliveries and budget checks affect the outcome. Budget checks are not atomic reservations and may allow overshoot; bookkeeping failures do not guarantee a hard cap. Pass `subtitles=true` on a YouTube social to include each video's transcript in the run results. Social media Social POST /api/socials/{id}/scrape

title: Agents
description: Verified email onboarding for a separate Recoup REST API key.
body:
## Use your real account

Prefer [MCP OAuth](/mcp-oauth) for supported AI hosts. REST integrations need a
separate API key; an OAuth connection does not export one into your shell.

Use the email verification flow below with an address the user controls. Keep
the returned key out of messages and logs, and store it through a secret facility
or an explicitly approved local environment file. Never use a disposable account
to recover an existing user's data.

The source signup contract also supports immediate keys for new `agent+` addresses.
That creates a separate identity; it does not grant customer or organization access.
It is not the recommended onboarding path for customer work. Multiple API keys per
account are supported, without revoking existing keys.

## Standard signup (email verification)

If you're building a human-facing integration and want the user to verify their real email, use an email address the user controls:

Step 1 — request a verification code:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/agents/signup" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "you@example.com"}'
```

Step 2 — submit the 6-digit code from the verification email:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/agents/verify" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "you@example.com", "code": "123456"}'
```

Response:

```json
{
  "account_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "api_key": "recoup_sk_abc123...",
  "message": "Verified"
}
```

## Using your API key

Pass the returned `api_key` in the `x-api-key` header on every authenticated request:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.recoupable.dev/api/tasks" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY"
```

See [Authentication](/authentication) for the full authentication model, including organization access and Bearer token support, and [Quickstart](/quickstart) for your first end-to-end request.
