title: Content Agent
description: Use hosted creative presets and current image, video and composition primitives.
body:
## Release Packs

For a song-centered content pack, use [Release Packs](/release-packs): collect
essential context inline, preserve one job, quote the complete scope and produce
reviewed media. New releases, catalog rediscovery, anniversaries, reissues and
remixes use the same brief-driven path. These pack operations do not require an
existing artist or repository; availability depends on deployed host tools.

## Hosted workflows

`POST /api/content/create` retains the hosted preset workflow. Supply the authorized
`artist_account_id`, optional `template`, `images`, `songs`, `batch` (defaults to 1; range 1–30), `lipsync`, `upscale`
and `caption_length`. Discover templates through `/api/content/templates` and its
detail route. The response contains `runIds`; poll `/api/tasks/runs?runId=...` until
terminal. Report failures and inspect the final artifact before delivery.

Hosted lipsync is a supported preset intent. The coordinated API/worker repair
restores the selected song window to the fixed audio-to-video path; that repaired
journey is release-pending until deployment and actual output verification.

## Direct primitives

For images use `POST /api/content/image` with `prompt` and up to 10 unique
`image_urls`. The house model is Muse Image, switching to its edit path when
references are present. New clients must use `image_urls`; compatibility aliases
are translated by the reconciliation release.

For video use `POST /api/content/video` with `prompt`, optional `image_url` and
`end_image_url`, integer `duration` 5–15, and `resolution` `480P` or `768P`.
The house model is MiniMax H3 Max. It has no six-mode selector, arbitrary model,
reference-only, extend, `video_url` or `audio_url` request control. Unsupported
semantic inputs return 400 in the reconciliation release, before paid generation.

The dedicated `/api/content/lipsync` primitive restores the existing fixed LTX
model for the worker; it is not assumed available on an older deployment.
Caption, transcribe, analyze, upscale and edit have their own endpoint contracts.
Local ffmpeg composition can crop, trim, overlay or mux a song; it does not create
mouth synchronization or prove a hosted generation succeeded.

## Cost and evidence

Each generation/inference stage can consume credits. `/api/content/estimate`
returns an advisory estimate, not a guaranteed price or complete final ledger.
A later failed composition does not imply that completed upstream work was free.
On insufficient credits, surface `billingUrl` and stop. Consult [Credits](/credits).

Record image inspection, motion review and audio playback. The worker checks for
an audio stream on lipsync output before composition; perceptual mouth alignment
still requires inspection. Automated checks do not replace human QA.

## Slack integration

The separate [Slack webhook](/api-reference/content-agent/webhook) handles
Content Agent mentions. Its request/event contract and the [completion callback](/api-reference/content-agent/callback) are distinct from direct primitives.
Workspace operators must configure the Slack application and service credentials;
installing a creative skill does not install that integration.

### Set up the Slack app

Create a Slack app, enable the `chat:write` and `app_mentions:read` bot scopes,
and subscribe to `app_mention` events at
`https://api.recoupable.dev/api/content-agent/slack`. Install it in the intended
workspace and invite it to the channel.

Configure `SLACK_CONTENT_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_CONTENT_SIGNING_SECRET`,
`CODING_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET` and `REDIS_URL` in the Recoup API service.
The existing Tasks worker uses the same `CODING_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET` for
completion callbacks and its authorized Recoup credential and API base URL.
Keep these values in service secret settings. The current callback secret name
is `CODING_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET`; `CONTENT_AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET` is obsolete.

Slack sends the signed-request headers listed in the [webhook reference](/api-reference/content-agent/webhook).
Keep `SLACK_CONTENT_SIGNING_SECRET` matched to that Slack app. Setup requests
with missing or invalid signatures, a timestamp outside the five-minute window,
or an unavailable signing secret return `401` with plain-text `Unauthorized`.
A verified setup request returns its JSON challenge. If setup fails, check the
app secret and service clock against [Slack request verification](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/verifying-requests-from-slack/).
Ordinary event acknowledgements come from the Slack adapter; they acknowledge
receipt while generation completes separately.

Mention the installed bot with the authorized artist account UUID:

```text
@RecoupContentAgent ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID artist-caption-bedroom batch=1
```

The template, `batch=N` (1–30) and `lipsync` flags are optional. Check the
acknowledgment, then inspect the completed result or reported failure in the
thread. Generated output still requires the inspection described above.

title: Release packs
description: Turn a song and a campaign occasion into a coherent set of reviewed music assets.
body:
<Info>
This contract accompanies the Release Packs first-use rollout. Availability depends
on the deployed API and the tools exposed by your connected host. A plugin download
or successful sign-in alone does not establish that generation is available.
</Info>

## Start with the music

Ask your agent: **“Create a release pack for this song.”** Supply the audio or an
accessible audio link. A listening page is not an audio file. Tell it whether this is a new release, an anniversary, a
reissue, a remix, or a catalog rediscovery campaign.

The agent reuses information you have already supplied and any selected, accessible
Recoup context. It asks only for essential gaps: the correct artist and recording,
the occasion, and artwork or creative direction. You can ask it to propose a
direction from the music instead. It must distinguish that proposal from your
established branding.

You do not need an existing artist profile, Spotify history, connected social
accounts, a catalog import, or a GitHub workspace to prepare a pack. An empty
Recoup roster is a valid new account. Sign in through your host's Recoup connection
when the agent needs authenticated execution; it should resume the same request.

**“Plan a release” is a different request.** It produces a creative brief and
rollout plan. Ask for a release pack to produce media, or ask for both so the agent
can carry the same brief into production.

When ChatGPT supplies a selected attachment to the upload tool, the tool accepts
its host file reference directly. It imports the selected download URL into
private Recoup storage and validates the actual media bytes. Other hosts can use
the supported source URL, inline or signed-upload modes; a filename alone is not
an accessible recording.

For direct API uploads, small inline files are limited to approximately 3 MB
(4,000,000 base64 characters). For normal song files, request a private signed
upload, transfer the file and finalize it, or import an accessible HTTPS source
up to 50 MiB for audio or 10 MiB for a reference image. Supported transfers depend on your host; an attachment is usable
only after the agent can access its actual bytes. Audio formats include MP3,
WAV, FLAC and M4A. Source images can be PNG, JPEG or WebP.

## What the brief contains

| Input | How it is used |
| --- | --- |
| Artist, song and exact version | Keep the recording, remix and artist identity consistent |
| Real audio and selected hook | Put the correct music into the finished clips |
| Occasion | Choose relevant concepts and copy rather than defaulting to “out now” |
| Creative direction or references | Keep a coherent visual family and voice |
| Primary action and destination | Write relevant captions without inventing links |
| Audience, platforms and constraints | Choose useful formats and respect supplied boundaries |

For anniversaries, the original release date and campaign date are separate. If
the original date is unknown, the agent must obtain it before making dated
anniversary claims. A catalog request needs a bounded selection of recordings;
it must not silently generate a pack for every track.

Research enriches the brief. Missing research or audience metrics should not
force unrelated onboarding or fabricated statistics. Existing artwork and
supplied preferences can be enough to propose strong creative work. An artist's
face is optional; artwork-led and typographic work are valid directions.

## Scope and budget before generation

### Save a direction and choose how involved to be

Connections exposing `brief.creative_context` can save an established visual world,
a rough idea or an exploratory direction in the same pack. The field is optional;
older connections keep their existing brief behavior. It holds attributed references,
up to three direction candidates and the selected candidate.

**Run with it** uses `working_mode: "autonomous"`: the agent records its direction
selection and continues within the approved budget. **Show me directions first**
uses `working_mode: "guided"`: final quoting and generation wait for a selection
recorded from the customer's feedback. An agent's own choice does not count as
customer selection in guided mode.

Save candidates under `directions`, then record `selection.direction_id`,
`selection.selected_by` (`customer` or `agent`) and a short `decision_note`.
Direction and reference IDs must be unique within this brief; selections cannot
point to another pack's candidate. Updating these fields follows the same saved
job and expected-revision rules and invalidates its earlier quote.

A reference manifest item declares its source, media type and `usage`:
`reference_only` is inspiration, while `production` explicitly makes an image
eligible as a selected generation input. Only production images referenced by
the chosen direction enter the renderer. Together with explicit legacy
`reference_image_urls`, at most five distinct production images are supported.
The original source manifest stays unchanged when production inputs are resolved.

The quote binds the current brief and deliverables. Changing the song or scope
requires a new quote; an earlier approval cannot silently authorize different work.

The pack retains its brief, revision, quote, individual asset states and completed

not make you repeat the request or regenerate the whole pack.

checkpoint. Progress distinguishes requested, generated, inspected and delivered

A finished music-bearing asset must contain the selected recording and the correct

visual consistency and the campaign brief. A render request, a prompt or a concept

permanent public knowledge-base entry automatically.

Connected operations are `prepare_release_pack`, `get_release_pack`,
`estimate_release_pack`, `generate_release_pack`, `retry_release_pack`,
`upload_release_pack_asset` and `export_release_pack`. Discover their actual schemas
in the connected host; older connections may need a refresh.

The shared API contract separates preparation, reading, quoting, generation,
retry and selected-asset upload. Connected tools use the same account and job
rules. Credentials remain with the host; an agent must not extract OAuth tokens
into REST requests or ask for an API key to compensate for a missing MCP tool.

If a required operation is unavailable, the agent should name that operation,
retain the brief and explain the next step. It must not claim the entire account
is disconnected or present a plan as completed media.

title: Task callback
description: Internal worker callback for a configured content agent. Requires the shared callback secret in x-callback-secret.
searchText:
Task callback  Internal worker callback for a configured content agent. Requires the shared callback secret in x-callback-secret.  Internal worker callback for a configured content agent. Requires the shared callback secret in x-callback-secret. Public content creation uses POST /api/content/create.

Internal callback endpoint for the `poll-content-run` Trigger.dev task. Receives content generation results and posts them back to the originating Slack thread. Authenticated via the `x-callback-secret` header.

This endpoint is not intended for external use — it is called automatically by the polling task when content runs complete, fail, or time out.

The receiver retains optional results[].imageUrl as a string, matching the existing videoUrl string validation; this does not add URL syntax validation. Only per-run results with status completed and a videoUrl enter media posting. An image without a completed video does not become an image-only job or still-only success. Existing video-only callbacks continue without an image read or image post.

For selected completed results, editorial images retain their per-result association and order; all editorial image posts precede all video posts, with videos also in result order. Images attach for normalized reported Content-Type image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/gif. Missing or unsupported reported MIME, or failed image download, falls back to an Editorial Image URL message before video posting continues. For an attachment filename, keep the final URL path component when it contains a dot; otherwise use editorial.<reported MIME extension>, with jpg for image/jpeg. Existing dotted filenames are not rewritten to match the MIME extension. Reported MIME is not byte verification or a safety scan. Each supplied image adds a media HTTP read and a thread attachment/link post within existing outbound callback trust, buffering and upload/runtime limits. This callback does not start another generation step or change generation billing.

Existing caption/video labels, failed-run summaries and terminal-thread retry skipping remain. The thread-state skip is not a concurrency-safe or exactly-once delivery guarantee. Normal image delivery requires both this receiver support and a deployed polling mapper that forwards imageUrl (API #1097 and Tasks #162). Source tests and this reference do not establish worker deployment, hosted authorization, actual Slack file rendering or end-to-end image delivery.

If the content bot is not configured, the route returns 503 with {error: "Content agent not configured"} before bot initialization, callback-secret handling or body parsing. For a configured bot, initialization precedes the handler; the handler checks x-callback-secret before parsing JSON or accessing a thread or media. Missing or invalid secrets return 401 with {status: "error", error: "Unauthorized"}. Invalid JSON returns 400 with {status: "error", error: "Invalid JSON body"}. Schema-validation 400 responses use status/error plus missing_fields, the first issue path containing string field names and numeric array positions (for example ["results", 0, "imageUrl"]). missing_fields is absent for malformed JSON.

A normal handler acknowledgement is 200 {status: "ok"}; a callback for an already-terminal thread is 200 {status: "ok", skipped: true} without another media post. These acknowledgements do not prove a Slack file was delivered or rendered. Handler 200/400/401 responses include the existing shared CORS headers; the unconfigured-bot 503 has no shared CORS headers. Shared response headers do not promise browser preflight success: x-callback-secret is not in the shared Access-Control-Allow-Headers list, and this route exports no OPTIONS handler. No stable 500 response envelope or delivery guarantee is declared here. Agents & sandboxes Content Agent POST /api/content-agent/callback

The repository comes from the [account's snapshot](/api-reference/sandboxes/list). Authenticate with `x-api-key` or an Authorization Bearer token.

Omit `account_id` to read the authenticated account. An explicit UUID must pass the existing account-access policy: the caller itself, an organization the caller belongs to, a shared-organization account, or existing Recoup administrative access. Invalid UUIDs return 400; denied targets return 403 before snapshot or repository lookup. A target read never falls back to the caller's repository. Successful explicit-target reads echo `account_id`; omitted-target responses do not add that field. This delegates reads only, not upload, replacement or deletion rights.

Clients selecting an account must send the same `account_id` on the list and file reads and require a matching response echo before using the result. Key cached data by authentication identity, target account and API origin. When that scope changes, reject stale in-flight results and invalidate writable revisions. Retain any unsaved replacement under its original account for manual recovery; never reuse that draft or its revision for a different account. An explicit override is a read-only view, even when it names the authenticated account. A SHA from a target read does not grant permission to write there.

To update an existing file without silently replacing a newer edit, set `include_revision=true`. The response pairs `content` with its blob `sha` from the same repository read. Keep that SHA with the opened draft and send it as `files[].expected_sha` when saving to the same account, resolved repository and path. Omitting the flag, or setting it to `false`, retains the legacy raw read without a SHA.

**Text files are returned verbatim. Recognized binary extensions (`.mp3`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.mp4`, `.pdf`, etc.) return base64 content with `encoding: base64`; decode those bytes before use.**

Versioned reads support existing regular files whose content is returned inline by the repository service (normally up to 1 MB). Unknown binary content that is not valid UTF-8 is rejected by the versioned read rather than converted into damaged text. Missing/unsupported content, directories and symlinks return an error.

The SHA identifies the file content; it is not an editing history. Agents & sandboxes Sandboxes GET /api/sandboxes/file

title: Upload files
description: Upload one or more files to the authenticated account's Git-backed repository. Each file URL is committed separately; paths inside a submodule resolve to that…
searchText:
Upload files  Upload one or more files to the authenticated account's Git-backed repository. Each file URL is committed separately; paths inside a submodule resolve to that…  Upload one or more files to the authenticated account's Git-backed repository. Each file URL is committed separately; paths inside a submodule resolve to that repository. Authenticate with `x-api-key` or an Authorization Bearer token.

For a guarded update of an existing file:
1. Read it with `GET /api/sandboxes/file?include_revision=true` and retain the returned `sha` with that draft.
2. Upload the edited bytes using the [staged-file upload](/api-reference/sandboxes/stage-file), then send the resulting URL and the original SHA as `files[].expected_sha`. Guarded updates save to `main`. A conflicting save is not retried automatically.
3. On a conflict, preserve the unsaved draft, reread the latest content and reconcile explicitly. Do not fetch a new SHA merely to force an older draft through.

A batch is not a transaction. HTTP 200 can include successful `uploaded` receipts alongside `errors` and `conflicts`; inspect every file. If every upload fails only because its condition conflicts, the response is 409. If all fail with mixed conflict/other failures, it is 500 and keeps the conflicts list. Conflicts contain submitted file names; successes include resulting blob SHAs.

Temporary upload blobs are deleted after every attempt, including conflicts, so retrying requires a new upload URL. Omitting `expected_sha` creates or updates the file on the repository default branch without checking the version you opened. The condition only supports updates to existing files. It protects saves that supply it; saving here does not update files in an already running sandbox.

If the target was deleted after the read, do not retry without the condition. This upload has no dedicated missing-target status: non-conflict failures return 500 when no file succeeds, or appear in `errors` alongside successful receipts in a 200 partial result. A missing target is not guaranteed to return 404 or 409; reread the path before deciding how to recover.

The optional `account_id` on list/file reads does not delegate uploads or replacements. This upload route remains bound to its existing authenticated-account ownership checks; do not reuse a different account's draft or SHA here. File deletion behavior is also unchanged. The chat UI polls this endpoint while showing the "loading sandbox…" state and flips to "ready" when `status` becomes `active`. The response includes `lifecycleVersion` (an optimistic concurrency token) and a `lifecycle` envelope with `serverTime`, the lifecycle FSM `state`, and timestamps for last activity, hibernation deadline, and sandbox expiry. As a side effect, if the runtime state is stale (expired or overdue for hibernation), the lifecycle workflow is kicked to clean up — callers do not need to do this themselves. Returns `card: null` when the selected customer has no supported default card, including when no tagged customer exists — the top-up dialog uses this to decide whether to show a pre-charge confirmation (card present) or route to a checkout session to collect one (`card: null`). title: Remove the payment method
description: Turn off automatic credit top-ups for the authorized account, then detach its selected default card.
searchText:
Remove the payment method  Turn off automatic credit top-ups for the authorized account, then detach its selected default card.  Turn off automatic credit top-ups for the authorized account, then detach its selected default card. This removes one card selected from the account's tagged Stripe customers; it does not delete every saved card. A successful request returns 204 with no response body. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to.

Other cards remain attached. A later `GET /api/accounts/{id}/payment-method` can return another remaining card; removal does not guarantee `card: null` or checkout-only purchases. A later explicitly requested credit purchase can use a remaining card, while an account with no card uses checkout. Removal does not turn automatic top-ups back on; enabling them again requires an explicit settings update.

The API saves `auto_topup_enabled: false` before detaching the selected card. If saving that setting fails, no card is detached. If settings are saved but detachment fails, automatic top-ups remain off and the request returns 500. Both failures return the same generic error, so read the payment method and auto-top-up settings to determine the current state. A missing customer or selected card returns 404 without changing settings or cards.

After an error or uncertain response, reread both states before deciding whether to retry. A successful removal may expose another selected card, so blindly repeating DELETE can remove a different card. Removal preserves balances, configured top-up amounts and thresholds, and other saved cards. It does not cancel subscriptions, invoices, a charge already in progress, or a concurrent explicit settings update. Accounts Payment methods DELETE /api/accounts/{id}/payment-method

Set the auto top-up settings for an account. All three fields are required on every call; there is no partial update. Turning it on requires a card on file (`GET /api/accounts/{id}/payment-method` returns a card), an amount between 5.00 and 1,000.00 USD, and a threshold below the amount. Turning it off keeps the last amount and threshold so the account can turn it back on without retyping them. Guardrails that apply once it is on: at most one top-up per account per 10 minutes; a card decline turns `enabled` back to `false`, records `lastError`, and emails the account instead of retrying; a successful selected-card removal turns it off before detachment, even when other saved cards remain. Removal does not cancel a charge already in progress. `id` may be the authenticated account or an organization the caller belongs to. Accounts Credits & usage PUT /api/accounts/{id}/auto-top-up

title: Create credits top-up session
description: Top up credits on the authenticated account.
searchText:
Create credits top-up session  Top up credits on the authenticated account.  Top up credits on the authenticated account.

**Credits are integer micro-dollars (1,000,000 = \$1.00, the same 6-decimal unit as USDC).** The customer is charged the USD value of `credits` plus a Stripe processing fee (US card pricing: 2.9% + \$0.30) — e.g. `credits: 100000000` charges \$103.30 total (\$100.00 credits + \$3.30 fee).

**Two outcomes, distinguished by response shape:**

- **Auto-charged** — if the account has a card on file (from a prior subscription or top-up), the card is charged immediately and the response is `{ paymentIntentId, creditsPurchased, totalCents }`. Credits land in the account's balance asynchronously via Stripe webhook (typically within seconds). No human interaction required.

- **Checkout required** — if no card is on file, or the saved card requires 3-D Secure authentication, the response is `{ id, url }` with a hosted Stripe Checkout URL. Redirect to that URL; credits land on successful payment.

Clients should discriminate on the presence of `url` (Checkout) vs `paymentIntentId` (auto-charged). Cards entered through the Checkout fallback are saved for future top-ups, so a customer's second top-up typically auto-charges. Accounts Credits & usage POST /api/credits/sessions

description: Read API-key record metadata associated with current account emails matching the case-insensitive agent+ prefix.
searchText:
List agent key metadata (admin) List agent key metadata Read API-key record metadata associated with current account emails matching the case-insensitive agent+ prefix. List agent-prefixed API-key metadata (Admin) Read API-key record metadata associated with current account emails matching the case-insensitive agent+ prefix. Authenticate with exactly one x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer credential for a Recoup admin account. Admin access is checked before query validation or metadata access.

Each returned record contains only id, name, email and created_at. id identifies an API-key record, not an account or credential; no API key value or hash is selected or returned. email is the first matching current associated email, not necessarily a primary or canonical address. Multiple matching emails do not multiply a key record; multiple keys on one account remain separate records. Deleted keys are absent; expired key records are not excluded. Current email associations can change. This is a current-email metadata selection, not evidence of origin from POST /api/agents/signup, a unique-agent/account count, active-key count, usage or adoption.

period defaults to all. Other values use inclusive midnight-UTC calendar boundaries on API-key record created_at: daily is today; weekly includes today and the preceding six calendar days; monthly includes today and the preceding 29 calendar days. Rows are ordered by key-record created_at descending. total is the length of the returned signups array, not a separate database-wide count. Existing database visibility and server row limits apply; no pagination or collection-completeness guarantee is provided. A successful empty read returns total 0 and signups []; a read failure returns a masked 500 instead.

This is GET /api/admins/agent-signups. The former GET /api/admins/agent/signups remains unavailable. The broader reporting decision in Mono #327 and original API #428 are not closed by this metadata route. Source tests use synthetic credential and storage boundaries; they do not prove production admin access, real data completeness or customer adoption. No UI, automatic caller, polling job, export or account/key creation is added. Accounts Admin accounts GET /api/admins/agent-signups

Powers the drilldown view that expands when a row in the [`/api/admins/credits/rollup`](/api-reference/admins/credits-rollup) table is opened. title: Grant credits (admin)
description: Sets an account's credit balance, and records who set it and why. Requires the authenticated account to be a Recoup admin.
searchText:
Grant credits (admin) Grant credits Sets an account's credit balance, and records who set it and why. Requires the authenticated account to be a Recoup admin.  Sets an account's credit balance, and records who set it and why. Requires the authenticated account to be a Recoup admin.

**Absolute, not a delta.** `remaining_credits` is the balance the account is left holding, whatever it held before — the outcome never depends on the balance at the moment the request lands. The prior balance comes back as `previous_credits` for the record. There is deliberately no add/subtract variant.

**Every grant is audited.** `reason` is required and must be non-empty. The grant is stored against the acting admin's account ID and is readable afterwards in the `grants` array of [`GET /api/admins/credits/events`](/api-reference/admins/credits-events).

**A grant is never reduced by the monthly refill.** Credit balances are topped up to the plan total by a monthly refill that runs lazily on the next read of [`GET /api/accounts/{id}/credits`](/api-reference/accounts/credits-get), once the underlying row is more than a month old. That refill is a floor, not an assignment: it raises a balance up to the plan total and never lowers one. A grant above the plan total therefore survives every refill and holds until it is spent, so headroom granted once stays granted and does not need re-granting on a schedule. Accounts Admin credits POST /api/admins/credits

title: Connection ownership
description: The connector connection-ownership and authority contract: who owns a connection, who can act through it, and why roster membership never grants execute rights.
body:
## Overview

Connectors link third-party services (Google Sheets, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, and others) to Recoup so agents can act on an artist's behalf. This page defines the **ownership and authority contract** for those connections: who a connection belongs to, and who is allowed to authorize, execute through, or disconnect it.

This contract is the source of truth for connector access control. Endpoint request and response shapes are documented separately in the [Connectors API reference](/api-reference/connectors/list).

---

## Association ≠ Authority

Artists in Recoup are **canonical and shared**. The same artist can appear in many accounts' rosters and in multiple organizations. Being associated with an artist is not the same as having authority to act through that artist's connections:

- An artist appearing in an account's roster (`account_artist_ids`) grants **read and analytics access only**.
- An artist appearing in an organization's roster likewise grants **read and analytics access only** to org members.
- Neither form of association ever grants the right to authorize, execute, or disconnect a connection.

<Warning>
Roster membership never inherits connection authority. If Account A connects an artist's TikTok, Account B having that same artist on its roster does **not** let Account B post through that connection.
</Warning>

---

## Connection Scope

Connections are scoped to the **relationship between an owner and an artist**, not to the bare canonical artist:

| Connection type | Scoped to |
|-----------------|-----------|
| Personal | The `(account, artist)` pair |
| Org-shared | The `(organization, artist)` pair |

The connection is keyed on the **join row** (the specific account-to-artist or org-to-artist relationship), never on the canonical artist alone. Two accounts that both roster the same artist hold two independent connection scopes for that artist.

**Whoever establishes a connection owns it.** Ownership is set at authorization time and does not transfer through roster changes.

Because artists stay canonical and shared, **isolation lives on the connection**: sharing an artist across accounts and orgs is safe precisely because each connection is confined to the relationship that created it.

---

## Authority Matrix

| Capability | Who has it |
|------------|-----------|
| Read / analytics on an artist | Any account or org member with the artist in their roster |
| Authorize a new connection | The account (or org member, for org-shared) establishing the connection, who then owns it |
| Execute actions through a connection | The owning account only; for org-shared connections, members of the owning org |
| Disconnect a connection | The owning account only; for org-shared connections, members of the owning org |
| Admin override | Recoup staff only (admins of the Recoup internal organization) |

<Note>
The admin override exists for support and abuse response. No customer account or organization, regardless of roster or org membership, can override another owner's connection.
</Note>

---

## Relationship to the Current API Reference

The [Connectors endpoint reference](/api-reference/connectors/list) currently describes connections as scoped to the authenticated account alone. That reflects behavior that shipped before this contract; the API is being re-keyed to the per-`(account, artist)` / per-`(organization, artist)` model defined here. Where the two disagree, **this page is the authority contract**. Endpoint docs will be updated as the re-keyed API ships.

Endpoint request and response shapes for the re-keyed model are deliberately not documented here yet.

title: Create post
description: Publish a video with its copy to one connected social account, now or at a set time.
searchText:
Create post  Publish a video with its copy to one connected social account, now or at a set time. Create post Publish a video with its copy to **one** connected social account, now or at a set time. Send one request per target account; to post the same video to several platforms, call this once per platform.

Without `publish_at` the post starts publishing immediately and is returned as `publishing`. With `publish_at` (a time in the future) it is returned as `scheduled`, starts publishing at that time, and can be cancelled until then with [Cancel Post](/api-reference/publishing/cancel). Either way this returns **202** right away: poll [Get Post](/api-reference/publishing/get) until `status` is `posted`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

The platform must already be connected for the artist in `artist_account_id`, or for the account itself when it is omitted (see [Authorize Connector](/api-reference/connectors/authorize)). Copy uses one shape for every platform. Which fields each platform uses, and their limits:

| Platform | `title` | `description` | `cover_url` | `privacy`, `tags` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `youtube` | **required**, video title, max 100 characters | video description, max 5,000 characters | not used (YouTube picks the frame) | used |
| `instagram` | not used | **required**, Reel caption, max 2,200 characters | Reel cover image | not used |
| `x` | not used | **required**, post text, max 280 weighted characters (URLs count as 23) | not used | not used |
| `linkedin` | video title shown on the post | **required**, post commentary, max 3,000 characters | video thumbnail | not used |

Limits are checked here, so an over-length body fails with 400 instead of at publish time.

Recoup applies no rate limit of its own to this endpoint. Each platform enforces its own caps, and a post over one ends `failed` with the platform's message in `error_message`:

| Platform | Cap |
|---|---|
| `instagram` | 100 API-published posts per account per 24 hours |
| `x` | the X API's per-app and per-user posting limits |
| `youtube` | the daily YouTube Data API upload quota of the connected Google project |
| `linkedin` | LinkedIn's daily per-member and per-organization API limits |

Each post costs **$0.01**, charged to the account the post is made in (`account_id`, or the calling account when omitted), never to the artist. The balance is checked here, so an account without enough credits gets **402** and no post is created. The charge is made only when the post reaches `posted`: a post that ends `failed` or `cancelled` is never charged. A scheduled post is checked against the balance when it is created and charged when it goes live. Connectors Publishing POST /api/posts

title: Check an application proposal
description: Validate proposed app addresses in your workspace without registering or activating an application.
body:
<Warning>
  Pending coordinated release. This checks a proposal; it does not register an
  app or make its origins trusted. Discover tool availability in your connected
  host before use.
</Warning>

Before connecting an external app, check its proposed name, environment, origins
and return URLs. A successful result means those values passed validation for
the selected workspace. It does not prove domain ownership.

## What happens

The preflight runs after normal Recoup authentication. First-time sign-in can
perform normal account provisioning and send its welcome email. After that,
this validator does not persist an application or issue application credentials.
It does not edit provider callbacks, create fan identities or sessions, allocate
capacity, or authorize purchases and spending.

`workspace_id` and `billing_owner_id` come from the authenticated account or an
organization it can access. They describe the proposed owner only. Supplying
`organization_id` does not grant workspace access. Do not submit account or
billing ownership overrides, secrets or tokens in the proposal.

The result is flat and includes `status: "validated"`, `persisted: false` and
`origins_verified: false`. It contains no application ID or token to install.

## Addresses and environments

- Choose `development` or `production` explicitly for each proposal.
- Use exact canonical origins such as `https://music.example`, without a trailing
  slash, wildcard, path, credentials, query or fragment. Different hosts and
  ports are different origins.
- HTTPS is required. Development also accepts HTTP on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`
  and `[::1]`; these loopback hosts are rejected in production.
- A return URL must be an exact canonical URL on one of the proposed origins,
  without credentials or fragments. For a bare host use its canonical trailing
  slash, such as `https://music.example/`. Query strings are retained literally.
- Each list takes 1–32 distinct addresses, each at most 2048 characters. The name
  is trimmed and must then contain 1–120 characters. These are input limits,
  not subscription or usage allowances.

Matching a return URL to a caller-proposed origin does not establish that the
caller owns either address. No DNS check, URL fetch or domain proof is performed.

## Standard MCP

On a standard API-key MCP connection that exposes `validate_application_registration`,
use the same proposal fields as HTTP. Account identity comes from the connection;
do not add `account_id` or extract a host-managed OAuth token.

```json
{
  "name": "Release companion",
  "environment": "production",
  "allowed_origins": ["https://music.example"],
  "return_urls": ["https://music.example/listen?connected=spotify"]
}
```

Delegated OAuth excludes this tool, including connections with `mcp:tools`.
HTTP and standard MCP share proposal validation; their transport-specific error
envelopes differ. HTTP authentication errors can use `error` or `message`, while
handled preflight errors use `status: "error"` and `error`. MCP failures are tool
errors or SDK input-validation errors. None confirms registration or activation.

See [authentication](/authentication) and [MCP connection guidance](/mcp).
Application persistence, origin proof/reverification, provider configuration,
fan bootstrap, suspension and quota policy require their own completed contracts.

title: Sites
description: Create, generate, and publish fan experiences through the API or MCP.
body:
Sites uses the same backend operations from the web app, HTTP API, and MCP. A new site is a **private draft**. Generation never publishes it automatically.

## Authentication

Private HTTP endpoints accept exactly one of `x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY` or `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
MCP uses the existing authenticated `https://api.recoupable.dev/mcp` connection.

The caller is derived from authentication. Do not send an `account_id`. An optional `organizationId` selects a workspace the caller can access. Omit it for the authenticated account's workspace.

## Endpoints and tools

| HTTP | MCP tool | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sites` | `list_sites` | `{ sites: [...] }` |
| `POST /api/sites` | `create_site` | `{ site: ... }`, HTTP 201 |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}` | `get_site` | `{ site: ... }` |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `concepts` | `propose_site_concepts` | Short pitches or missing context |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `generate` | `generate_site` | Generate from an optional customer-selected pitch; otherwise select a concept |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `generation` | `get_site_generation` | Status for the specified generation token |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `publish` | `publish_site` | Publish the saved draft or the playable build selected by `generationToken` |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `unpublish` | `unpublish_site` | Public snapshot removed, draft retained |
| `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` action `delete` | `delete_site` | `{ "deleted": true, "id": "..." }` |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/signups` | `get_site_signups` | `{ signups: [{ email, created_at }] }`, up to 10,000 |
| `POST /api/sites/assets` | `upload_site_asset` | `{ asset: { url, name, type } }` |

Listing accepts optional `organizationId` and `artistId` query parameters. All private reads and writes verify workspace access. Signup emails are never part of the public response.

## Create and generate

Create a draft with a Spotify track, album, or playlist URL. Recoup retrieves its title and artwork. The brief is optional; without it, Recoup uses the available song and artist context to propose activities. Alternatively, supply both a name and a brief without a release URL.

```bash
curl https://api.recoupable.dev/api/sites \
  -H "x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"releaseUrl":"https://open.spotify.com/track/TRACK_ID","brief":"Build a maze game"}'
```

Optional creation fields: `name` (120 characters), `brief` (6,000), `organizationId`, `artistId`, and `assets` (up to eight workspace-owned assets returned by the upload endpoint). An artist must be accessible to the caller and belong to the selected organization when one is used.

Read `site.id` and `site.revision`, then start automatic generation:

```json
{"action":"generate","revision":0}
```

For Spotify tracks, the background workflow saves metadata, acquires and verifies full audio, saves Music Flamingo lyrics and musical analysis, collects artwork observations and public artist research, compiles a saved brief, selects a concept, and builds and reviews the site. No separate collector calls are required. Audio acquisition requires a Spotify preview for waveform verification and stops if no matching full recording is found. Completed accepted context is reused.

To choose a concept yourself before generation, optionally request pitches:

```json
{"action":"concepts","revision":0}
```

Send this to `PATCH /api/sites/{id}`, or call MCP `propose_site_concepts` with `id` and `revision`. Optional `instruction` and `contextBriefId` apply to pitching too. This can use credits for context collection and a pitch call, but does not create images, site code or change the draft.

The response is `{ concepts: { status, candidates, reason }, revision }`. Status is `ready`, `needs-context`, or `no-good-concept`. Metadata and cover details alone return `needs-context`; provide usable song analysis or sourced artist context rather than forcing an activity out of the artwork.

In the explicit-selection flow, show the short pitches to the customer and wait for their choice. Each candidate contains `name`, `activity`, `fanMotivation`, `songOrArtistConnection`, and `friendHook`. Pass the selected object unchanged as `approvedConcept`:

```json
{
  "action": "generate",
  "revision": 0,
  "approvedConcept": {
    "name": "CUSTOMER_SELECTED_NAME",
    "activity": "SELECTED_ACTIVITY",
    "fanMotivation": "SELECTED_MOTIVATION",
    "songOrArtistConnection": "SELECTED_CONNECTION",
    "friendHook": "SELECTED_HOOK"
  }
}
```

MCP `generate_site` accepts the same fields plus `id`, without `action`. A customer-authored concept is also accepted. The optional `approvedConcept` preserves a caller-selected activity. When omitted, the engine selects from its proposed concepts after collecting context.

Generation defaults to background execution and returns a generation token; poll `get_site_generation` (HTTP action `generation`) for the result. Set `background: false` only for a synchronous client that supports a long timeout. If review rejects the concept, the draft is marked `needs-review`; the system does not silently substitute a new activity. Asset and implementation repairs retain their bounded pass.

Generation failures identify the stopped stage and leave the saved draft unchanged. A `409` means another edit changed the revision; read the site again before retrying.

### Poll background generation

Send this JSON body to `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` using the token returned by the
generation request. MCP `get_site_generation` takes `id` and `token`, without `action`.
Polling uses `token`; publishing and cancellation use `generationToken`.

```json
{"action":"generation","token":"TOKEN_FROM_GENERATION"}
```

The token is bound to its site and caller and expires. Invalid, expired or
mismatched tokens return 404 during token verification; a missing or empty token
is invalid input (400). A running job is not proof that a
playable build or a published page exists; read the returned status and progress.

## Generate from saved Context Engine evidence

Save a single-song `creative_direction` brief using the Context Engine `save_brief` action, then pass its snapshot ID when requesting pitches:

```json
{
  "action": "concepts",
  "revision": 0,
  "contextBriefId": "SAVED_BRIEF_UUID"
}
```

Pass the same `contextBriefId` with the selected `approvedConcept` to generation. It is available on both MCP `propose_site_concepts` and `generate_site`. Without a saved brief, track generation automatically collects and saves context, reusing compatible accepted module results. The brief must belong to the site's workspace and match its Spotify track. Sites rejects unavailable or superseded snapshots before generation. Revisions reuse the draft's selected brief unless a new ID is supplied.

This path reuses accepted song summaries, artwork observations, public artist research and release/artist metadata instead of collecting them again. The creative director and generator receive attribution, coverage and missing-topic information. Supported evidence includes public Spotify metadata/artwork, YouTube-attributed audio analysis and saved public-search research. Private uploads, customer assertions and raw lyrics are excluded. Matching saved machine transcripts inform paraphrased themes but are not forwarded to the site. Partial evidence stays partial.

Generation still uses credits for creative direction, assets, implementation and review. It saves a private draft, never publishes automatically. Snapshot availability is checked again before saving and publishing. Later source withdrawal does not automatically retract an already published site. Internal evidence and source identifiers are excluded from the public site response.

## Publish

After reviewing the intended draft or preview, publish through the same PATCH
endpoint or MCP `publish_site`, using the site's current saved revision.

Publishing automatically prepares Spotify fan connection for an active paid workspace. The standard agreement uses the attributed artist's name; the customer does not need a separate setup step. Missing artist attribution or unavailable Spotify configuration stops paid publication with an actionable error. Publication requires an eligible paid workspace. The gate checks the site's owning workspace for an active subscription with a positive-priced item; a trial or Pro entitlement alone does not establish eligibility. Unpaid publication returns HTTP 402 before publishing. Successful paid setup reports `fanConnection: "enabled"`.

For a custom hosted destination, HTTP callers may include `returnUrl` (an HTTPS URL without credentials or fragment) in the publish body. Otherwise an existing connection destination is preserved, or the configured Sites public origin is used. The Recoup editor supplies its actual published URL. The authenticated fan-connection API remains available for external integrations.

The public page is `https://chat.recoupable.dev/s/{id}`.

### Publish the saved draft

Use the current revision from the saved site (3 in this example):

```json
{"action":"publish","revision":3}
```

Omitting `generationToken` selects the saved draft, even when a background job has
a newer preview. MCP `publish_site` takes `id` and `revision`, without `action`.

### Publish a working preview

To publish a specific working preview from a background generation, pass its
token as `generationToken` and the site's current saved revision:

```json
{"action":"publish","revision":3,"generationToken":"TOKEN_FROM_GENERATION"}
```

MCP `publish_site` uses the same fields plus `id`, without `action`. The token must
match the site and caller. The selected build must contain a completed playable
build step for the current site/workspace/revision; the whole generation job need
not already be completed. A preview that is not ready returns 400, a stale build
returns 409, and invalid or expired token access returns 404. A temporary saved-build
failure may return 503. Without `generationToken`, publication uses the saved draft;
it does not automatically select the newest background preview.

### Entitlement required

An ineligible workspace receives HTTP 402 with an error body, for example:

```json
{"error":"Site publishing is unavailable with this workspace's current entitlements. The draft is preserved."}
```

Keep the draft and explain that publishing is unavailable. Plugin workflows do
not offer plans, link to checkout or start a purchase. Resume only after access
is independently available and the user requests publication again. This
response does not publish the site or create a checkout session.

### Unpublish

Send `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` with the current revision to remove the public
snapshot while retaining the draft. MCP `unpublish_site` takes `id` and `revision`.

```json
{"action":"unpublish","revision":3}
```

Agents should publish, unpublish or delete only when explicitly instructed.

## Delete and cancel generation

Delete only when explicitly instructed. Send `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` with `action: "delete"` and the current `revision` in its JSON request body (Content-Type: application/json). Include `generationToken` when cancelling a known in-progress generation. The token must belong to this site and caller; cancellation is attempted before deletion. Omitting it does not request cancellation of every running job.

For example, use the current saved revision and the token returned by a known generation:

```json
{"action":"delete","revision":3,"generationToken":"TOKEN_FROM_GENERATION"}
```

Omit generationToken when no known generation needs cancellation.

Deletion checks workspace access and revision, then returns `{ "deleted": true, "id": "..." }`. A stale revision returns 409; reload before retrying. Unpublish with `action: "unpublish"` when the draft should remain available.

## Uploads

HTTP uploads are multipart forms with a `file` field and optional `organizationId` query parameter. Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, MP3, and WAV, up to 4 MB per file. Images are re-encoded to WebP. Audio is checked for its file signature.

MCP's `upload_site_asset` accepts `name`, `contentType`, `base64` file bytes, and optional `organizationId`. It uses the same validation and storage path as HTTP.

## Public endpoints

- `GET /api/sites/public/{id}` returns `{ snapshot: ... }` for a published site only. Drafts, account identifiers, and signup data are excluded.
- `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/signup` accepts `{"email":"fan@example.com","consent":"yes"}`. An optional `website` honeypot must be empty. Duplicate submissions succeed without disclosing list membership. Unpublished sites reject signups.

Public pages and the browser music player render in the chat app. The API provides
snapshots, generation, uploads, signup persistence and the fan-connection integration
routes listed below.

## Route coverage

The lifecycle and public snapshot/signup operations above are documented here in
prose; they are not a complete Sites OpenAPI specification. The following existing
routes are accounted for as integration surfaces, outside the copyable lifecycle
examples. Listing them does not establish live authorization or add an MCP tool.

### Authenticated integration routes

| HTTP | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/fan-connection` | Read fan-connection configuration |
| `PUT /api/sites/{id}/fan-connection` | Configure the fan connection through the authenticated integration |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/fans` | Fan reporting |
| `GET /api/sites/{id}/activity` | Activity reporting |

### Browser integration routes

| HTTP | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sites/apple/config` | Browser music configuration |
| `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/activity` | Published-site activity collection |
| `GET /api/sites/public/{id}/spotify` | Show the fan-connection acceptance page |
| `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/spotify` | Begin Spotify authorization after acceptance |

These browser flows are not replacements for a private lifecycle request or proof
of a completed fan connection. Email signup and Spotify connection are distinct.

### Provider callback

`GET /api/sites/spotify/callback` completes the provider redirect flow. It is
intentionally excluded from agent lifecycle examples; do not invoke it as a
standalone operation. OPTIONS preflight handlers are also excluded from the
operation tables because they serve browser CORS negotiation.

## Errors

- `402`: publication requires an eligible paid workspace.

`400` invalid input; `401` missing/invalid authentication; `403` workspace or artist access denied; `404` missing/unpublished site; `409` stale revision; `422` Spotify metadata unavailable; `503` temporary operation failure.

The selected build must contain a completed playable build step for the current site/workspace/revision; the whole generation job need not already be completed. A preview that is not ready returns 400, a stale build returns 409, and invalid or expired token access returns 404. A temporary saved-build failure may return 503. Without `generationToken`, publication uses the saved draft; it does not automatically select the newest background preview. ### Entitlement required An ineligible workspace receives HTTP 402 with an error body, for example: Keep the draft and explain that publishing is unavailable. Plugin workflows do not offer plans, link to checkout or start a purchase. Resume only after access is independently available and the user requests publication again. This response does not publish the site or create a checkout session. ### Unpublish Send `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` with the current revision to remove the public snapshot while retaining the draft. MCP `unpublish_site` takes `id` and `revision`. Agents should publish, unpublish or delete only when explicitly instructed. ## Delete and cancel generation Delete only when explicitly instructed. Send `PATCH /api/sites/{id}` with `action: "delete"` and the current `revision` in its JSON request body (Content-Type: application/json). Include `generationToken` when cancelling a known in-progress generation. The token must belong to this site and caller; cancellation is attempted before deletion. Omitting it does not request cancellation of every running job. For example, use the current saved revision and the token returned by a known generation: Omit generationToken when no known generation needs cancellation. Deletion checks workspace access and revision, then returns `{ "deleted": true, "id": "..." }`. A stale revision returns 409; reload before retrying. Unpublish with `action: "unpublish"` when the draft should remain available. ## Uploads HTTP uploads are multipart forms with a `file` field and optional `organizationId` query parameter. Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, MP3, and WAV, up to 4 MB per file. Images are re-encoded to WebP. Audio is checked for its file signature. MCP's `upload_site_asset` accepts `name`, `contentType`, `base64` file bytes, and optional `organizationId`. It uses the same validation and storage path as HTTP. ## Public endpoints - `GET /api/sites/public/{id}` returns `{ snapshot: ... }` for a published site only. Drafts, account identifiers, and signup data are excluded. - `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/signup` accepts `{"email":"fan@example.com","consent":"yes"}`. An optional `website` honeypot must be empty. Duplicate submissions succeed without disclosing list membership. Unpublished sites reject signups. Public pages and the browser music player render in the chat app. The API provides snapshots, generation, uploads, signup persistence and the fan-connection integration routes listed below. ## Route coverage The lifecycle and public snapshot/signup operations above are documented here in prose; they are not a complete Sites OpenAPI specification. The following existing routes are accounted for as integration surfaces, outside the copyable lifecycle examples. Listing them does not establish live authorization or add an MCP tool. ### Authenticated integration routes | HTTP | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `GET /api/sites/{id}/fan-connection` | Read fan-connection configuration | | `PUT /api/sites/{id}/fan-connection` | Configure the fan connection through the authenticated integration | | `GET /api/sites/{id}/fans` | Fan reporting | | `GET /api/sites/{id}/activity` | Activity reporting | ### Browser integration routes | HTTP | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `GET /api/sites/apple/config` | Browser music configuration | | `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/activity` | Published-site activity collection | | `GET /api/sites/public/{id}/spotify` | Show the fan-connection acceptance page | | `POST /api/sites/public/{id}/spotify` | Begin Spotify authorization after acceptance | These browser flows are not replacements for a private lifecycle request or proof of a completed fan connection. Email signup and Spotify connection are distinct. ### Provider callback `GET /api/sites/spotify/callback` completes the provider redirect flow. It is intentionally excluded from agent lifecycle examples; do not invoke it as a standalone operation. OPTIONS preflight handlers are also excluded from the operation tables because they serve browser CORS negotiation. ## Errors - `402`: publication requires an eligible paid workspace. `400` invalid input; `401` missing/invalid authentication; `403` workspace or artist access denied; `404` missing/unpublished site; `409` stale revision; `422` Spotify metadata unavailable; `503` temporary operation failure.

title: Connect Spotify fans to a site
description: Configure paid fan connection from an artist agent and retrieve fans attributed to its site.
body:
Release dependency: these routes require the site fan connection API release and its database migration. The skill alone does not enable them. Base URL: `https://api.recoupable.dev`.

Private calls use `x-api-key: $RECOUP_API_KEY` (or the platform's existing bearer authentication). Customer credentials stay with the agent/server. Public connection entry and callback use browser-bound OAuth state, not the customer API key.

## Customer and site

- `GET /api/accounts/id`: verify the current credential.
- `POST /api/agents/signup` with `{ "email": "customer@example.com" }`: request email verification.
- `POST /api/agents/verify` with `{ "email": "customer@example.com", "code": "123456" }`: receive `api_key`; never echo it.
- `GET /api/artists`: inspect the caller's roster and choose the artist's account ID.
- `GET /api/sites`: inspect existing site records.
- `POST /api/sites` with `{ "name": "Release experience", "artistId": "ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID", "releaseUrl": "https://open.spotify.com/track/TRACK_ID" }`: register a site. Add `organizationId` only for a selected authorized workspace. Read the returned `site.id`. Omit owner/account ID fields; ownership comes from authentication.

## Configure

`GET /api/sites/{siteId}/fan-connection` returns:

```json
{
  "siteId": "SITE_UUID",
  "ownerId": "WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT_UUID",
  "artistId": "ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID",
  "config": null,
  "connectUrl": null
}
```

Existing `config` contains `site_id`, `return_url`, `marketing_text`, `enabled` and `revision`. Update with `PUT /api/sites/{siteId}/fan-connection`:

```json
{
  "returnUrl": "https://artist.example/release",
  "marketingText": "I agree to receive release announcements and offers by email from Example Artist.",
  "enabled": true,
  "revision": 0
}
```

Use the real artist's approved text, not the example unchanged. Return URL must be HTTPS, at most 2048 characters, without credentials or fragments. Text length is 20–1000 characters. Pass the last read revision, or 0 for initial configuration. The response has the same envelope with persisted config and the public `connectUrl`; always use that returned URL.

- 400: invalid input or missing artist attribution.
- 401/403: reconnect the customer or select an authorized workspace.
- 402: no eligible paid subscription for the site's owning account.
- 404: missing site or API not deployed; inspect the actual response.
- 409: another configuration update won; reload and reconcile before retry.
- 503: provider, billing or storage unavailable; surface the dependency.

Spotify fan connection uses an existing eligible entitlement owned by the site's
workspace. No separate add-on is required and fans do not buy this feature.
On 402, the error is `"Fan connection is unavailable with this workspace's current entitlements."`.
Preserve the site and configuration. Plugin workflows explain the limit without
plan promotion, payment links, card setup or purchase. Do not retry activation
automatically; resume only after access is independently available and the user
asks to continue.

## Public fan journey

`GET /api/sites/public/{siteId}/spotify` displays the site's agreement. Its own form POST binds acceptance to that browser and configuration revision, then redirects to Spotify PKCE authorization. Do not handcraft this POST or bypass the page. Spotify returns to Recoup's `/api/sites/spotify/callback`; Recoup then returns to the configured site URL with `recoup_spotify=connected`, `cancelled` or `failed`.

Only a successful provider exchange with `user-read-email` and `user-read-private` creates records. Actual granted scopes and the exact accepted marketing text are retained separately from the successful connection. Email may be absent. No tokens or profile details are passed to the public site.

## Read fans

`GET /api/sites/{siteId}/fans?offset=0&limit=50` (private):

```json
{
  "fans": [],
  "total": 0,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 50
}
```

Each fan has `id`, `site_id`, `spotify_id`, `display_name`, `email`, first/last connection timestamps and nested `site_fan_connections` with `site_fan_permissions` and `site_fan_marketing_consents`. Paginate up to 100 fans per page. Records are private to authorized workspace members. Read access remains available after paid eligibility expires. Repeated connection updates the existing fan for that site and adds a connection history entry. The site's owner and artist supply attribution. These records are separate from email-only signups and other artist audience data.

Starter Checkout can return HTTP 400 `starter_unavailable` when its price is not
configured. Explain the unavailable option and use a configured plan; do not retry
it as a transient provider failure.

## Recoup operator setup

Operators must apply `20260928010000_site_fan_connections.sql`, configure `SITES_SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, register an HTTPS callback ending `/api/sites/spotify/callback`, set `SITES_FAN_SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI`. This is Recoup service configuration, not work to impose on each artist. The existing browser playback callback remains separate.

## Activity reporting

`GET /api/sites/{siteId}/activity` returns 30-day counts for visits, starts, completions, replays and shares to authorized workspace members. `POST /api/sites/public/{siteId}/activity` accepts `{id: EVENT_UUID, visitId: VISIT_UUID, event: "visit" | "start" | "complete" | "replay" | "share"}`. Reuse the event UUID when retrying. Use a site-scoped visit ID. Never send emails, profile data or arbitrary page contents to this endpoint. These are browser-reported interactions, not verified Spotify listening or a named fan activity history.

Recoup-hosted generated sites use the trusted host bridge: `window.recoup.track(event)` reports approved events; `window.recoup.join()` reveals the trusted signup controls. External sites should implement the equivalent fixed-event transport and keep account credentials on the server.

## Playback for Premium and Free listeners

The hosted player reads the connected Spotify profile's `product` field. Premium listeners use the Spotify Web Playback SDK. Free (`free` or `open`) listeners use the site's saved, verified recording through the same play/pause, seek and volume controls. If the profile cannot be read, its subscription remains unknown; available artist audio keeps playback usable. The player also handles a Spotify SDK account rejection by switching to the recording.

`GET /api/sites/public/{siteId}` includes `playbackAudioUrl`, a fresh signed audio URL valid for one hour, or `null` when no matching verified recording is available. It is resolved from the published site's workspace-owned context request and matching Spotify track; private research and analysis are excluded. Fetch a fresh public response when reloading rather than storing this URL permanently. Publish only audio you have permission to serve to fans.

File playback is not a Spotify stream. Spotify playback subscription, Recoup's paid fan-connection entitlement, and fan capture are separate concerns. A missing audio file must show an honest unavailable state while keeping the game playable.

title: One player for every release
description: Create a listening page or embed Spotify and Apple Music playback on your artist website.
body:
Create a player for a song, album or Spotify playlist. Share its listening page or embed it on your website. Recoup handles music-service sign-in, supported browser playback and fan activity reporting.

## Create and publish

Use the [Recoup API](/api-reference/players/create) or the `create_release_player` MCP tool. Choose an artist you can access, name the player, and provide a `spotifyUrl`, an `appleUrl`, or both. Use `organizationId` to create it in your organization workspace.

For website embeds, add the exact website origins to `allowedOrigins`. An origin includes the scheme, hostname and any non-default port, such as `https://artist.example:8443`. Embed origins must use HTTPS. Include both the www and non-www origins if fans can visit either. You can omit this field when sharing only the hosted listening page.

Example create request:

```json
{
  "artistId": "ARTIST_ACCOUNT_UUID",
  "organizationId": "ORGANIZATION_UUID",
  "name": "Release title",
  "spotifyUrl": "https://open.spotify.com/album/ALBUM_ID",
  "appleUrl": "https://music.apple.com/us/album/release/APPLE_ID",
  "allowedOrigins": ["https://artist.example", "https://www.artist.example"]
}
```

New players start unpublished. Review the music links, then publish with `update_release_player`, passing `id`, the current `revision`, and `enabled: true`. Publishing requires an active paid Recoup workspace.

Use the same tool to change the music links, title, artwork or approved website origins. Pass the current revision returned by Recoup with each update. The player stays assigned to its original artist and workspace. Updating it ends existing player sessions, so fans may need to reconnect.

See [update a release player](/api-reference/players/update) for the REST request and fields.

## Share a listening page

Use the returned `listenUrl` as your bio or campaign link. No custom website is needed. Fans choose from the music services configured for that player.

To track campaign traffic, add `source`, `medium`, `campaign`, and `content` query parameters. The listening page also accepts `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, and `utm_content`. Use campaign labels, such as `instagram` and `release`; keep personal information out of links.

## Embed on your website

Use the returned `spotifyEmbedUrl` or `appleEmbedUrl` for each configured service. The `parent` parameter must match an approved website origin.

```html
<iframe
  src="https://app.recoupable.dev/listen/PLAYER_UUID/spotify?parent=https%3A%2F%2Fartist.example&source=instagram&campaign=release"
  title="Recoup music player"
  allow="autoplay; encrypted-media"
></iframe>
```

Keep music-service sign-in inside the Recoup player. Your website does not need Spotify or Apple credentials. Include a direct music-service link as a fallback when browser playback is unavailable.

For Spotify Free handoffs, the embed sends a `recoup:open-dsp` message with `provider: "spotify"`. Your website must verify that the message comes from the Recoup player origin and that iframe's window, then open the Spotify destination configured for the player. Do not use a destination URL supplied by a message.

## What fans can play

Spotify Premium fans can stream through the browser player after connecting. Spotify playlist players show a selectable song list and highlight the current song. Selecting a song starts playback at its position in the playlist. Unavailable entries cannot be selected. If the list fails to load, fans can retry or open the playlist in Spotify.

Spotify Free fans are sent to the configured song, album or playlist in Spotify after connecting. Spotify controls whether that opens in its app or website and which playback options the fan has. If Recoup cannot confirm the account's subscription, it does not assume the account is Free.

Apple Music playback uses the fan's Apple Music authorization and subscription. Apple sessions do not capture email or create an identified fan contact in Recoup.

## Optional uploaded audio for Spotify Free fans

You can choose to let Spotify Free fans play an uploaded audio file in Recoup instead of sending them to Spotify. Set `freePlayback: "audio"` and provide `audioUrl`. This setting belongs to the player owner; fans cannot change it. Premium fans continue to stream from Spotify.

Upload an MP3 or WAV through `POST /api/sites/assets` in the same workspace, then use the returned `asset.url`. The current upload limit is 4 MB. Audio mode requires a Spotify destination as a fallback.

MCP arguments for `update_release_player`:

```json
{
  "id": "PLAYER_UUID",
  "revision": 1,
  "freePlayback": "audio",
  "audioUrl": "WORKSPACE_UPLOADED_ASSET_URL"
}
```

For REST, send `PATCH /api/players/PLAYER_UUID` with the same body except `id`; the player ID belongs in the URL.

Audio mode plays one uploaded file per player. It does not support an uploaded playlist or generate Spotify streams. Uploaded-file playback is excluded from the player's music-service playback reports; fan connections are still recorded. If the file is missing, fans are sent to Spotify. If it fails to load, the player offers an Open in Spotify link.

To restore the Spotify handoff, set `freePlayback: "spotify"`. You can also clear `audioUrl` by setting it to `null`.

## Fan contacts belong to your workspace

Spotify sign-in captures the profile information and email that Spotify makes available. A returning Spotify account reuses its contact in the same workspace.

If that fan connects to another artist in your workspace, Recoup adds an artist relationship to the same contact. If they connect in another organization, that organization gets a separate contact. Your contact and listening history stay in your workspace. Matching names or email addresses alone do not merge fans.

- Use `get_workspace_player_fans` or [read workspace player fans](/api-reference/players/workspace-fans) to list contacts and their artist relationships.
- Use `get_release_player_fans` or [read artist player fans](/api-reference/players/fans) to list fan relationships across that artist's players in the workspace.

`contact_id` identifies the workspace contact. Each artist relationship has its own `id`; activity records refer to that relationship as `fan_id`.

Spotify sign-in does **not** grant email marketing consent. Use a separate, optional signup before sending marketing emails. Apple Music sessions remain anonymous and are not linked to Spotify contacts.

## Measure listening activity

Use `get_release_player_activity` or [read listening activity](/api-reference/players/activity) for 30-day campaign totals and individual track, play, pause and skip events.

These reports describe activity observed while the Recoup player is open. Playback after a fan leaves for Spotify or Apple Music is outside these reports. Player events and reported listening time are **not confirmed music-service stream counts** and do not prove that a campaign caused additional streams. Compare them with catalog stream measurements to evaluate campaign performance.

## Check your fan journey

Before promoting the link, test it on the phones and social browsers your fans use. Confirm that sign-in works, the correct music opens, playlist songs can be selected, and the Spotify Free fallback works. Then check fan and activity reports in the intended workspace.

Compare them with catalog stream measurements to evaluate campaign performance. ## Check your fan journey Before promoting the link, test it on the phones and social browsers your fans use. Confirm that sign-in works, the correct music opens, playlist songs can be selected, and the Spotify Free fallback works. Then check fan and activity reports in the intended workspace.
